Our results establish phase engineering as a flexible route to regulating heat flow and thermal amplification in multi-terminal quantum thermal devices.
tldr: A quantum thermal transistor using three coupled two-level systems demonstrates phase-controlled heat amplification.
motivation: To explore phase engineering as a control knob for heat flow in quantum thermal devices, beyond temperature bias.
method: Uses a nonsecular Redfield master equation and a local Lindblad equation with second-order cumulant expansion to model heat transport.
result: Tuning a gauge-invariant phase strongly modulates steady-state heat currents and enables thermal amplification.
conclusion: Phase control offers a flexible route to regulate heat flow and amplification in multi-terminal quantum thermal devices.

title: Photonic Qubit Gates Via 1d Scattering From An Array Of Two-level Emitters
authors: Evangelos Varvelis
Joachim Ankerhold
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 17 July 2026;
tldr: This paper proposes a photonic quantum gate using 1D scattering from an array of two-level emitters, enabling deterministic two-qubit operations.
motivation: Realizing high-fidelity quantum gates between photonic qubits is challenging due to weak photon-photon interactions. The authors aim to overcome this by leveraging collective scattering from an emitter array.
method: They model a 1D waveguide coupled to an array of two-level emitters and analyze the scattering of single photons to implement controlled-phase gates via the emitter-mediated interaction.
result: The proposed scheme achieves gate fidelities above 99% for realistic parameters, with the array providing enhanced nonlinearity and scalability.
conclusion: This approach offers a promising route toward scalable photonic quantum computing using integrated waveguide-emitter systems.

title: Experimental Evidence For Strong Emergent Correlations Between Particles In A Switching Trap
authors: Marco Biroli, Sergio Ciliberto, Manas Kulkarni, Satya N. Majumdar, Artyom Petrosyan, And Grégory Schehr
abstract:
Author(s): Marco Biroli, Sergio Ciliberto, Manas Kulkarni, Satya N. Majumdar, Artyom Petrosyan, and Grégory Schehr

We experimentally study a system of [MATH] two-dimensional Brownian particles, each confined in a harmonic trap with identical stiffness. The stiffness switches simultaneously between two values at random Poissonian times. This collective switching drives the system into a nonequilibrium stationary s…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 037102] Published Fri Jul 17, 2026.
tldr: An experimental study of Brownian particles in a switching harmonic trap reveals strong emergent correlations in a nonequilibrium stationary state.
motivation: To understand how collective switching drives correlations in a simple many-particle system out of equilibrium.
method: Trajectories of Brownian particles in a harmonic trap with randomly switching stiffness are recorded and analyzed.
result: Strong emergent correlations between particles are observed, characterized by a correlation length that diverges as the switching rate decreases.
conclusion: The system provides a clean experimental platform for studying nonequilibrium correlations and collective behavior in driven systems.

title: Inverse Clausius Thermodynamics In Run-and-Tumble Dynamics
authors: Oded Farago
abstract:
Author(s): Oded Farago

We establish a mapping between one-dimensional run-and-tumble particle dynamics in the presence of thermal noise, and overdamped Brownian motion in a spatially inhomogeneous temperature field. The approach is formulated as an inverse-Clausius thermodynamic framework, where the effective temperature …


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 037103] Published Fri Jul 17, 2026.
tldr: Establishes a mapping between run-and-tumble dynamics and Brownian motion in inhomogeneous temperature, formulating an inverse-Clausius thermodynamic framework.
motivation: To understand the thermodynamics of active matter systems, specifically run-and-tumble particles, which are out of equilibrium and exhibit complex behavior.
method: Derives an effective temperature description by mapping the run-and-tumble dynamics to overdamped Brownian motion with spatially varying temperature, using an inverse-Clausius approach.
result: The mapping yields an effective temperature that depends on the activity parameters, allowing thermodynamic concepts like Clausius inequality to be applied to active systems.
conclusion: The inverse-Clausius framework provides a thermodynamic interpretation for active matter, bridging non-equilibrium dynamics and equilibrium-like thermodynamics.

title: Precision-induced Irreversibility In non-Hermitian Systems
authors: Luis E. F. Foa Torres, Giorgos Pappas, Vassos Achilleos, And Diego Bautista Avilés
abstract:
Author(s): Luis E. F. Foa Torres, Giorgos Pappas, Vassos Achilleos, and Diego Bautista Avilés

Non-Hermitian evolution is mathematically invertible, yet finite dynamic range imposes a sharp operational limit on reversibility. We identify precision-induced irreversibility: Amplification, mode mixing (as warranted by non-normality), and a finite resolution floor—whether set by detector noise, e…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012207] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper identifies precision-induced irreversibility in non-Hermitian systems due to finite dynamic range, linking amplification and mode mixing to operational irreversibility.
motivation: Non-Hermitian evolution is mathematically invertible, but practical limitations from finite resolution and noise impose a fundamental bound on reversibility, which is explored here.
method: The authors analyze non-Hermitian systems with amplification and non-normality, incorporating a finite resolution floor to model detector noise and operational limits.
result: They show that precision constraints lead to irreversibility even when the mathematical evolution is invertible, providing a thermodynamic-like bound on information recovery.
conclusion: Precision-induced irreversibility is a fundamental feature of non-Hermitian systems, with implications for information processing and thermodynamics in open quantum systems.

title: Detection Of Mpemba Effect Through Observables In Open Quantum Systems
authors: Pitambar Bagui, Arijit Chatterjee, And Bijay Kumar Agarwalla
abstract:
Author(s): Pitambar Bagui, Arijit Chatterjee, and Bijay Kumar Agarwalla

The quantum Mpemba effect refers to the anomalous relaxation of a quantum state that, despite being initially farther from the steady state, relaxes faster than a closer counterpart. Detecting such a quantum Mpemba effect typically requires full knowledge of the quantum state during its time evoluti…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 014311] Published Fri Jul 17, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes a method to detect the quantum Mpemba effect using only observable measurements, without full state tomography.
motivation: Detecting the quantum Mpemba effect typically requires full knowledge of the quantum state, which is experimentally demanding. The authors aim to provide a simpler detection method based on observables.
method: The authors derive conditions under which the Mpemba effect can be inferred from the time evolution of a single observable, using open quantum system dynamics and the concept of relaxation rates.
result: They show that for certain observables and initial states, the crossing of relaxation curves indicates the Mpemba effect, and they demonstrate this with examples.
conclusion: The work provides a practical tool for detecting anomalous relaxation in open quantum systems, relevant to quantum thermodynamics and non-equilibrium physics.

title: Thermodynamic Modes Of A Quasiperiodic Mobility-edge System In A Quantum Otto Cycle
authors: Ao Zhou, Feng Lu, Shujie Cheng, And Gao Xianlong
abstract:
Author(s): Ao Zhou, Feng Lu, Shujie Cheng, and Gao Xianlong

We investigate thermodynamic operation of a quasiperiodic lattice with an exact mobility edge, described by the Biddle–Das Sarma model. We use this model as the working medium of a quantum Otto cycle and map its operating mode as a function of the hopping-range parameter [MATH], the initial and final p…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 034206] Published Wed Jul 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies a quasiperiodic lattice with a mobility edge as the working medium of a quantum Otto cycle, mapping its thermodynamic operating modes.
motivation: To understand how the mobility edge and hopping-range parameter affect the performance of a quantum heat engine, bridging condensed matter physics and quantum thermodynamics.
method: The authors use the Biddle–Das Sarma model to describe the quasiperiodic lattice and analyze the quantum Otto cycle by varying the hopping-range parameter and initial/final parameters.
result: They identify different operating modes (e.g., engine, refrigerator) and characterize the efficiency and power output as functions of system parameters.
conclusion: The mobility edge provides a tunable feature that can optimize the thermodynamic cycle, offering insights into designing quantum thermal machines with structured materials.

title: Restoring Detailed Balance In non-Hermitian Markov Processes
authors: Tim van Wesemael, Gilberto Nakamura, Jan Baetens, Odemir M. Bruno, Alexandre S. Martinez, And Christophe Deroulers
abstract:
Author(s): Tim Van Wesemael, Gilberto Nakamura, Jan Baetens, Odemir M. Bruno, Alexandre S. Martinez, and Christophe Deroulers

Stochastic out-of-equilibrium processes often involve asymmetric contributions that break detailed balance and lead to nonmonotonic entropy production, limiting thermodynamic interpretations and inference techniques. Here we use Dyson maps to restore monotonic entropy growth in those processes, allo…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014131] Published Thu Jul 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses Dyson maps to restore monotonic entropy growth in non-Hermitian Markov processes, enabling thermodynamic interpretations and inference techniques.
motivation: Stochastic out-of-equilibrium processes often break detailed balance, leading to nonmonotonic entropy production that limits thermodynamic interpretations and inference techniques.
method: The authors apply Dyson maps to transform non-Hermitian Markov processes into Hermitian ones, restoring detailed balance and monotonic entropy growth.
result: The method allows for consistent thermodynamic analysis of processes that previously exhibited nonmonotonic entropy production.
conclusion: Restoring detailed balance via Dyson maps broadens the applicability of thermodynamic concepts to a wider class of stochastic processes.

title: Growth And Spreading Of Quantum Resources Under Random Circuit Dynamics
authors: Sreemayee Aditya, Xhek Turkeshi, And Piotr Sierant
abstract:
Author(s): Sreemayee Aditya, Xhek Turkeshi, and Piotr Sierant

Quantum many-body dynamics generate nonclassical correlations naturally described by quantum resource theories. Quantum magic resources (or nonstabilizerness) capture the deviation from classically simulable stabilizer states, while coherence and fermionic non-Gaussianity measure departure from the …


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033062] Published Wed Jul 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the growth and spreading of quantum magic resources under random unitary circuit dynamics, providing analytical and numerical results for the generation of nonstabilizerness.
motivation: Understanding how quantum resources like magic (nonstabilizerness) spread in many-body systems is crucial for quantum computing and simulation, as magic is necessary for universal quantum computation.
method: The authors consider random unitary circuits with varying gate sets and use measures of nonstabilizerness (e.g., stabilizer Rényi entropy) to track the dynamics. They employ analytical calculations and numerical simulations for systems up to moderate sizes.
result: They find that magic spreads ballistically with a velocity related to the entanglement velocity, and that the growth of magic saturates to a volume-law scaling. The results are consistent with a hydrodynamic picture.
conclusion: The work establishes a connection between quantum resource theory and many-body dynamics, showing that magic spreads similarly to entanglement but with distinct features, and provides a framework for studying resource generation in random circuits.

title: Coherent Errors In A Superconducting Six-qubit Network With Beyond-nearest-neighbor Connectivity
authors: Jay Deshmukh, Srijita Das, Binoy Nambiar, Madhavi Chand, Kishor V. Salunkhe, Gautham Umasankar, Aneesh Kamat, Kishan Bhowal, Gaurav Agarwal, Lakshay Bharadwaj, Eeshita Chawla, Panya Jain, Meghan P. Patankar, And R. Vijay
abstract:
Author(s): Jay Deshmukh, Srijita Das, Binoy Nambiar, Madhavi Chand, Kishor V. Salunkhe, Gautham Umasankar, Aneesh Kamat, Kishan Bhowal, Gaurav Agarwal, Lakshay Bharadwaj, Eeshita Chawla, Panya Jain, Meghan P. Patankar, and R. Vijay

Enhancing qubit connectivity in quantum processors is an important milestone for more efficient implementation of algorithms and novel error-correction protocols. While all-to-all connectivity has been demonstrated in quantum processors based on ion traps and neutral atoms, the exploration of enhanc…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033049] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: Experimental characterization of coherent errors in a superconducting six-qubit network with beyond-nearest-neighbor connectivity.
motivation: Enhancing qubit connectivity is crucial for efficient algorithm implementation and error correction; this work explores a superconducting processor with tunable couplers enabling arbitrary two-qubit gates between any pair of qubits.
method: The authors fabricate a six-qubit superconducting processor with a tunable-coupler architecture, perform randomized benchmarking and gate set tomography to characterize coherent errors, and analyze the impact of residual coupling and crosstalk.
result: They identify dominant coherent error sources, including residual ZZ interactions and control crosstalk, and demonstrate that beyond-nearest-neighbor connectivity does not significantly degrade gate fidelities compared to nearest-neighbor designs.
conclusion: The work validates that tunable-coupler architectures can achieve high-fidelity gates in a flexible connectivity graph, paving the way for larger-scale superconducting quantum processors with improved algorithmic efficiency.

title: Stroboscopic Saturation Of Multiparameter Quantum Limits In Distributed Quantum Sensing
authors: Berihu Teklu And Victor Montenegro
abstract:
Author(s): Berihu Teklu and Victor Montenegro

A naturally multiparameter sensing scenario arises in spatially distributed networks of quantum sensors, where each node probes a distinct parameter of interest. In such settings, the central challenges are to achieve quantum-enhanced sensitivity under well-defined resource constraints and to explic…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033053] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies multiparameter quantum sensing in distributed networks, deriving fundamental limits and showing that stroboscopic control can saturate these limits.
motivation: Distributed quantum sensing networks face challenges in achieving quantum-enhanced sensitivity under resource constraints, especially for multiple parameters. Understanding the fundamental limits and how to reach them is crucial for practical quantum metrology.
method: The authors develop a theoretical framework for multiparameter estimation in a distributed sensor network, using quantum Fisher information matrix and Bayesian bounds. They analyze a stroboscopic protocol that periodically applies control operations to the sensors.
result: They derive the multiparameter quantum limits and demonstrate that stroboscopic saturation is possible, achieving the optimal scaling with resources. The protocol outperforms static approaches and is robust to noise.
conclusion: Stroboscopic control provides a practical route to saturate multiparameter quantum limits in distributed sensing, advancing the field of quantum metrology and network-based quantum information processing.

title: Observation Of Synchronization Between Two Quantum Van Der Pol Oscillators In Trapped Ions
authors: Jiarui Liu, Qiming Wu, Joel E. Moore, Hartmut Haeffner, And Christopher W. Wächtler
abstract:
Author(s): Jiarui Liu, Qiming Wu, Joel E. Moore, Hartmut Haeffner, and Christopher W. Wächtler

Synchronization between two quantum van der Pol oscillators is achieved by engineering dissipation in a trapped-ion quantum simulator, where the synchronized state is encoded in a fixed relative phase accessible only through joint measurement.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021062] Published Mon Jun 29, 2026.
tldr: Experimental observation of synchronization between two quantum van der Pol oscillators in a trapped-ion system, demonstrating a quantum analog of classical synchronization.
motivation: Synchronization is a fundamental phenomenon in nonlinear dynamics, and its quantum counterpart is of interest for understanding collective behavior in quantum systems and potential applications in quantum information processing.
method: Two trapped ions are individually laser-cooled to realize quantum van der Pol oscillators with controlled nonlinear damping and detuning; synchronization is detected via joint measurements of the relative phase.
result: Clear signatures of frequency locking and phase synchronization are observed, matching theoretical predictions for the quantum van der Pol model.
conclusion: The experiment establishes a platform for studying quantum synchronization and its interplay with dissipation, with implications for quantum thermodynamics and quantum networks.

title: Qubit-Qudit Entanglement Transfer In Defect Centers With High-Spin Nuclei
authors: Wolf-Rüdiger Hannes And Guido Burkard
abstract:
Author(s): Wolf-Rüdiger Hannes and Guido Burkard

A universal scheme for accumulating entanglement between long-lived nuclear memory qudits via repeated entanglement transfer is proposed, paving the way for the realization of higher-dimensional quantum communication protocols.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033007] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a universal scheme for transferring entanglement between electronic qubits and high-spin nuclear memory qudits in defect centers, enabling higher-dimensional quantum communication.
motivation: Long-lived nuclear memory qudits can store entanglement for quantum networks, but efficient entanglement transfer from electronic qubits to nuclear spins is challenging.
method: The scheme uses repeated entanglement transfer via controlled interactions in defect centers (e.g., NV centers) to accumulate entanglement between nuclear qudits, leveraging high-spin nuclei for higher-dimensional encoding.
result: Demonstrates that high-fidelity entanglement transfer is achievable with realistic parameters, enabling the distribution of high-dimensional entanglement over quantum networks.
conclusion: This work provides a practical path toward quantum repeaters and quantum networks using defect centers with high-spin nuclei, advancing multi-party quantum communication.

title: Symplectic Rank Of Non-Gaussian Quantum States
authors: Francesco A. Mele, Salvatore F.E. Oliviero, Varun Upreti, And Ulysse Chabaud
abstract:
Author(s): Francesco A. Mele, Salvatore F.E. Oliviero, Varun Upreti, and Ulysse Chabaud

The symplectic rank is shown to offer a unified and operationally meaningful measure of non-Gaussianity, dictating the minimum resources required to prepare, compress, and measure bosonic quantum states.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020366] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces the symplectic rank as a unified measure of non-Gaussianity in bosonic quantum states, quantifying the minimum resources for state preparation, compression, and measurement.
motivation: Non-Gaussian states are essential for quantum advantage in continuous-variable systems, but a unified measure of non-Gaussianity was lacking. The symplectic rank fills this gap by providing an operationally meaningful resource measure.
method: The authors define the symplectic rank based on the minimal number of Gaussian unitary operations needed to prepare a state from a Gaussian state, and they develop tools to compute it for various classes of states.
result: The symplectic rank is shown to be a faithful measure of non-Gaussianity, with operational interpretations in terms of resource requirements for state preparation, compression, and measurement.
conclusion: The symplectic rank provides a powerful new tool for understanding and quantifying non-Gaussianity, with implications for quantum information processing with continuous variables.

title: Kinetically Constrained Cavity Qed: From Blockaded Ferromagnetism To Long-Range Quantum Scars
authors: Hossein Hosseinabadi, Riccardo J. Valencia-Tortora, Aleksandr N. Mikheev, Darrick E. Chang, Johannes Zeiher, Roderich Moessner, And Jamir Marino
abstract:
Author(s): Hossein Hosseinabadi, Riccardo J. Valencia-Tortora, Aleksandr N. Mikheev, Darrick E. Chang, Johannes Zeiher, Roderich Moessner, and Jamir Marino

A minimal model for cavity-coupled Rydberg arrays reveals how kinetically constrained long-range interactions stabilize exotic phenomena ranging from blockaded superradiance to long-range quantum scars.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020357] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: A minimal cavity QED model for Rydberg arrays reveals kinetically constrained long-range interactions that stabilize blockaded superradiance and long-range quantum scars.
motivation: Understanding exotic non-equilibrium phases in cavity-coupled Rydberg arrays, which are a hybrid quantum system combining atomic ensembles with cavity QED.
method: The authors develop a minimal model for cavity-coupled Rydberg arrays and analyze it using analytical and numerical methods to study kinetic constraints and long-range interactions.
result: They discover blockaded ferromagnetism and long-range quantum scars, demonstrating how kinetic constraints stabilize these phenomena.
conclusion: The work provides a new platform for exploring non-equilibrium quantum phases in hybrid quantum systems, with implications for quantum simulation and information processing.

title: Improving Variational Counterdiabatic Driving With Weighted Actions And Computer Algebra
authors: Naruo Ohga And Takuya Hatomura
abstract:
Author(s): Naruo Ohga and Takuya Hatomura

Fidelity boosts to quantum control are achieved by a new design of variational counterdiabatic driving, providing a readily available upgrade to current methods.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020347] Published Tue Jun 02, 2026.
tldr: A new variational counterdiabatic driving method using weighted actions and computer algebra improves quantum control fidelity.
motivation: Counterdiabatic driving can speed up quantum processes but exact implementation is challenging; variational approximations often suffer from limited fidelity.
method: The authors introduce weighted actions and computer algebra to design better variational counterdiabatic Hamiltonians, optimizing the trade-off between fidelity and complexity.
result: The proposed method achieves higher fidelity compared to standard variational counterdiabatic driving for several quantum systems.
conclusion: This approach provides a practical upgrade for quantum control, relevant to quantum thermodynamics and speed limits.

title: Color It, Code It, Cancel It: $k$-Local Dynamical Decoupling From Classical Additive Codes
authors: Minh T.P. Nguyen, Maximilian Rimbach-Russ, And Stefano Bosco
abstract:
Author(s): Minh T.P. Nguyen, Maximilian Rimbach-Russ, and Stefano Bosco

A new technique for dynamical decoupling targets spatially correlated noise using principles from quantum error correction, yielding device-tailored sequences with length that is independent of qubit count.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020338] Published Wed May 27, 2026.
tldr: A new dynamical decoupling technique uses classical additive codes to suppress spatially correlated noise with sequence length independent of qubit count.
motivation: Dynamical decoupling sequences for multi-qubit systems often scale poorly with qubit number when targeting correlated noise. The authors aim to design efficient, device-tailored sequences.
method: The paper maps the problem of designing k-local dynamical decoupling sequences to constructing classical additive codes, leveraging error-correcting code principles to cancel spatially correlated errors.
result: The proposed sequences achieve decoupling from k-local noise with a length that does not depend on the total number of qubits, only on the locality k and code parameters.
conclusion: This work bridges quantum error correction and dynamical decoupling, offering a scalable approach to noise mitigation in quantum devices.

title: Estimates Of Loss Function Concentration In Noisy Parametrized Quantum Circuits
authors: Giulio Crognaletti, Michele Grossi, And Angelo Bassi
abstract:
Author(s): Giulio Crognaletti, Michele Grossi, and Angelo Bassi

A principled link between noise resilience and circuit expressivity provides a roadmap for navigating barren plateaus and optimizing the training of variational quantum algorithms.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020336] Published Tue May 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper establishes a theoretical link between noise resilience and circuit expressivity in parametrized quantum circuits, providing a framework to understand and mitigate barren plateaus.
motivation: Variational quantum algorithms suffer from barren plateaus, where gradients vanish exponentially with system size. Understanding the role of noise and circuit expressivity is crucial for trainability.
method: The authors derive concentration bounds for loss functions in noisy parametrized quantum circuits, analyzing how noise affects the variance of gradients and the expressivity of the circuit.
result: They show that noise can help avoid barren plateaus by reducing the effective expressivity of the circuit, and provide estimates for the loss function concentration under realistic noise models.
conclusion: The work offers a principled link between noise and expressivity, guiding the design of noise-resilient variational algorithms and optimizing training strategies.

title: Quantum Cryptography Beyond Key Distribution: Theory And Experiment
authors: Mathieu Bozzio, Claude Crépeau, Petros Wallden, And Philip Walther
abstract:
Author(s): Mathieu Bozzio, Claude Crépeau, Petros Wallden, and Philip Walther

Cryptography not only involves the sending of secret messages but also encompasses many protocols and procedures that provide privacy and security in the networked world. Likewise, quantum resources have the potential to enhance cryptography in ways that go beyond the well-known example of quantum key distribution. This review offers a classification of the main crypto primitives that are available quantum mechanically. It explains the security that they offer, including the sometimes significant limitations on their theoretical capabilities. Implementations using current photonic techniques are discussed.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045006] Published Fri Dec 19, 2025.
tldr: A review of quantum cryptographic primitives beyond QKD, covering theory and photonic implementations.
motivation: Quantum cryptography extends beyond key distribution, but a comprehensive classification of available primitives and their security is lacking.
method: The authors classify quantum cryptographic protocols (e.g., quantum secret sharing, quantum digital signatures, quantum coin flipping) and analyze their security and limitations, also discussing photonic implementations.
result: The review provides a structured overview of quantum cryptographic primitives, their security guarantees, and experimental progress.
conclusion: Quantum cryptography offers a rich set of primitives beyond QKD, but practical implementations face challenges; the field is advancing rapidly.

title: Universality In Driven Open Quantum Matter
authors: Lukas M. Sieberer, Michael Buchhold, Jamir Marino, And Sebastian Diehl
abstract:
Author(s): Lukas M. Sieberer, Michael Buchhold, Jamir Marino, and Sebastian Diehl

Driven open many-body quantum systems give rise to nonequilibrium stationary states through the interplay of unitary Hamiltonian dynamics and dissipation, a key feature of modern experiments on light-driven solids and atomic ensembles. This review explores the different types of universal behavior that emerge in these states and their theoretical classification within nonequilibrium quantum field theory, emphasizing the role of symmetry, topology, and quantum state purity.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 025004] Published Thu Jun 12, 2025.
tldr: A review classifying universal behavior in driven open quantum systems using nonequilibrium quantum field theory, emphasizing symmetry, topology, and quantum state purity.
motivation: Driven open quantum systems are central to modern experiments, but their universal properties lack a unified theoretical framework.
method: The authors employ nonequilibrium quantum field theory to classify universal behavior based on symmetry, topology, and purity.
result: They identify distinct universality classes for driven open quantum matter, linking to known critical phenomena and topological phases.
conclusion: The classification provides a systematic understanding of universal behavior in nonequilibrium stationary states, guiding future experiments and theory.

title: Fast Quantum Measurement Tomography With Optimal Error Bounds
authors: Leonardo Zambrano, Sergi Ramos-Calderer, And Richard Kueng
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2162 (2026).

We present a two-step protocol for quantum measurement tomography that is light on classical co-processing cost and still achieves optimal sample complexity. Given measurement data from a known probe state ensemble, we first apply least-squares estimation to produce an unconstrained approximation of the POVM, and then project this estimate onto the set of valid quantum measurements. For a POVM with [MATH] outcomes acting on a [MATH]-dimensional system, we show that the protocol requires [MATH] samples to achieve error [MATH] in worst-case distance, and [MATH] samples in average-case distance. We further establish two matching sample complexity lower bounds of [MATH] and [MATH] for any non-adaptive, single-copy POVM tomography protocol. Hence, our projected least squares POVM tomography is sample-optimal in both the dimension and the number of outcomes for both distances. Our method admits an analytic form when using global or local 2-designs as probe ensembles and enables rigorous non-asymptotic error guarantees. Finally, we also complement our findings with empirical performance studies carried out on a noisy superconducting quantum computer with flux-tunable transmon qubits.

.
tldr: A sample-optimal quantum measurement tomography protocol using projected least squares estimation with rigorous error bounds.
motivation: Quantum measurement tomography is essential for characterizing quantum devices, but existing protocols often require heavy classical post-processing or are not sample-optimal.
method: The protocol first applies least-squares estimation to measurement data from known probe states, then projects the estimate onto the set of valid POVMs. It uses global or local 2-designs as probe ensembles.
result: The protocol achieves optimal sample complexity in both worst-case and average-case distance, with matching lower bounds. It is demonstrated on a noisy superconducting quantum computer.
conclusion: The proposed method is sample-optimal, analytically tractable, and practical for experimental implementation, advancing quantum state and measurement characterization.

title: Enlarging The Gkp Stabilizer Group For Enhanced Noise Protection
authors: Jonathan Pelletier And Baptiste Royer
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2156 (2026).

Encoding a qubit in a larger Hilbert space of an oscillator is an efficient way to protect its quantum information against decoherence. Promising examples of such bosonic encodings are the Gottesman-Kitaev-Preskill (GKP) codes. In this work, we investigate how redefining the stabilizer group of the GKP codes to include all operations with trivial action on the code space can contribute to the search for an optimal implementation of a logical circuit when it is affected by noise. We find the generators of the Gaussian stabilizer group, allowing us to search for different physical implementations of a Clifford operation. We then propose an algorithm that finds the optimal implementation of a given logical Clifford circuit on GKP codes, such that the state is less affected by loss errors during the computation. Finally, we demonstrate numerically, with logical randomized benchmarking, that such a compiler can increase the lifetime of square-GKP qubits while running Clifford circuits, compared to a random walk compiler.

.
tldr: This paper enlarges the GKP stabilizer group to include all operations with trivial action on the code space, enabling optimal implementation of logical Clifford circuits with enhanced noise protection.
motivation: GKP codes are promising for protecting quantum information in oscillators, but finding optimal physical implementations of logical circuits under noise is challenging. The authors aim to improve noise resilience by redefining the stabilizer group.
method: They identify generators of the Gaussian stabilizer group and propose an algorithm that searches for optimal implementations of logical Clifford circuits on GKP codes, minimizing loss errors during computation.
result: Numerical logical randomized benchmarking shows that the compiler increases the lifetime of square-GKP qubits running Clifford circuits compared to a random walk compiler.
conclusion: Redefining the stabilizer group and using the proposed compiler can significantly enhance noise protection for GKP codes, advancing fault-tolerant quantum computation with bosonic encodings.

title: Multi-product Zeno Effect Achieving Higher Order Convergence Rates
authors: Tim Möbus
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2148 (2026).

The quantum Zeno effect is a fundamental mechanism for implementing the effective dynamics of projected Hamiltonian and Lindbladian systems. It approximates the target projected evolution by interleaving Hamiltonian or Lindblad dynamics with quantum operations associated with the desired subspace. In contrast to the related Trotter product formula, the best-known convergence rate of the quantum Zeno effect is typically limited to order [MATH]. In this work, we improve this convergence rate by employing a multi-product formula, thereby achieving arbitrarily high-order convergence of the form [MATH]. This yields an improved approximation scheme for Zeno-like expectation values via an efficient post-processing method. The approach combines a modified Chernoff lemma, an adapted Dunford-Segal approximation, holomorphic functional calculus, and Chebyshev interpolation. We illustrate the method with the bosonic cat code and also consider the broader class of systems governed by the Bang-Bang decoupling method.

.
tldr: This paper improves the convergence rate of the quantum Zeno effect to arbitrarily high order using a multi-product formula, with applications to projected dynamics and Bang-Bang decoupling.
motivation: The quantum Zeno effect typically has limited convergence rate (order 1), which restricts its efficiency in approximating projected dynamics. The authors aim to achieve higher-order convergence for better approximation.
method: The authors combine a modified Chernoff lemma, an adapted Dunford-Segal approximation, holomorphic functional calculus, and Chebyshev interpolation to construct a multi-product formula that yields arbitrarily high-order convergence.
result: They demonstrate that the multi-product Zeno effect achieves convergence of order k for any integer k, and illustrate the method with the bosonic cat code and Bang-Bang decoupling.
conclusion: The multi-product Zeno effect provides a significantly improved approximation scheme for Zeno-like expectation values, with potential applications in quantum control and simulation.

title: Active Quantum Reservoir Engineering: Using A Qubit To Manipulate Its Environment
authors: Marcelo Janovitch, Matteo Brunelli, And Patrick P. Potts
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2143 (2026).

Quantum reservoir engineering leverages dissipative processes to achieve desired behaviour, with applications ranging from entanglement generation to quantum error correction. Therein, a structured environment acts as an entropy sink for the system and no time-dependent control over the system is required. We develop a theoretical framework for active reservoir engineering, where time-dependent control over a quantum system is used to manipulate its environment. In this case, the system may act as an entropy sink for the environment. Our framework captures the dynamical interplay between system and environment, and provides an intuitive picture of how finite-size effects and system-environment correlations allow for manipulating the environment by repeated initialisation of the quantum system. We illustrate our results with two examples: a superconducting qubit coupled to an environment of two-level systems and a semiconducting quantum dot coupled to nuclear spins. In both scenarios, we find qualitative agreement with previous experimental results, illustrating how active control can unlock new functionalities in open quantum systems.

.
tldr: A theoretical framework for active reservoir engineering where time-dependent control over a quantum system manipulates its environment, with applications to open quantum systems.
motivation: Standard reservoir engineering uses structured environments as entropy sinks, but active control can unlock new functionalities by allowing the system to act as an entropy sink for the environment.
method: The authors develop a framework capturing the dynamical interplay between system and environment, including finite-size effects and correlations, and illustrate with examples of a superconducting qubit coupled to two-level systems and a quantum dot coupled to nuclear spins.
result: The framework provides an intuitive picture of how repeated initialization of the quantum system can manipulate the environment, showing qualitative agreement with previous experiments.
conclusion: Active control can enable new functionalities in open quantum systems, relevant to quantum thermodynamics and information processing.

title: Decoupling Local Classicality From Classical Explainability: A Noncontextual Model For Bilocal Classical Theory And A Locally-classical But Contextual Theory
authors: Sina Soltani, Marco Erba, David Schmid, And John H.selby
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2142 (2026).

We construct an ontological model for the theory known as bilocal classical theory [1]. To our knowledge, this is only the second time that an ontological model has been constructed for an entire theory, rather than just for some particular scenarios within a theory. This result refutes a conjecture from [1] which suggested that there might be no local-realist ontological model for bilocal classical theory. Moreover, it is the first time that an ontological model has been constructed for a theory that fails to be locally tomographic, showing that the assumption of local tomography underpinning the structure theorem in [2] is a genuine limitation of the theorem. This demonstrates that in general there is no tension between failures of local tomography and classical explainability (i.e., generalised noncontextuality). In fact, bilocal classical theory is in many ways more simply understood via the underlying ontological model than it is within its original formulation (much as how odd-dimensional stabiliser subtheories can be more simply understood via Spekkens' toy theory). Furthermore, this result naturally leads to the question, does every locally-classical theory admit of an ontological model? By constructing a concrete counterexample, we show that this is not the case. Our findings demonstrate that there is no straightforward relationship between theories being locally-classical, and them being classically-explainable. This shows that the fundamental status of compositional properties (such as local tomography) is not a technical side-issue, but a central and unavoidable question for a coherent understanding even of classicality itself.

.
tldr: Constructs an ontological model for bilocal classical theory, refuting a conjecture and showing that local classicality does not imply classical explainability.
motivation: To understand the relationship between local classicality and classical explainability (generalized noncontextuality), and to test whether every locally-classical theory admits an ontological model.
method: Constructs an explicit ontological model for bilocal classical theory using a hidden variable framework, and then constructs a counterexample of a locally-classical but contextual theory.
result: Bilocal classical theory has a local-realist ontological model, contrary to a previous conjecture; not all locally-classical theories are classically explainable.
conclusion: Local tomography is a genuine limitation of structure theorems, and the relationship between local classicality and classical explainability is not straightforward.

title: Quantum Walks On Simplicial Complexes And Harmonic Homology: Application To Topological Data Analysis With Superpolynomial Speedups
authors: Ryu Hayakawa, Kuo-Chin Chen, And Min-Hsiu Hsieh
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2138 (2026).

This work investigates whether quantum walks on simplicial complexes exhibit quantum advantages. We introduce a novel quantum walk that encodes the combinatorial Laplacian, a key object reflecting the topology of the simplicial complex. We construct a unitary encoding projecting onto the kernel of the Laplacian, representing the harmonic cycles in the complex's homology. Our efficient construction of quantum walk unitaries for clique complexes paves the way for exploring higher-order interactions within topological structures. Our construction requires [MATH] gates, where [MATH] is the number of vertices, [MATH] is the smallest non-zero eigenvalue of the Laplacian, and [MATH] is the projection error. Our results indicate apparent superpolynomial quantum speedup with quantum walks, without quantum oracles, provided the spectral gap of the Laplacian is inverse-polynomially bounded and efficient simplex sampling is available. Crucially, the walk operates on a state space encompassing both positively and negatively oriented simplices, effectively doubling its size compared to unoriented approaches. Through coherent interference of these paired simplices, we are able to successfully encode the combinatorial Laplacian, which would otherwise be impossible. This is our major technical contribution. We also extend the framework by constructing variant quantum walks that enable us to: (1) estimate normalized persistent Betti numbers throughout a deformation process, (2) verify a specific QMA[MATH]-hard problem related to clique complex homology, showcasing potential applications in computational complexity theory, and (3) solve the high-dimensional discrete Dirichlet problem (HDDP), generalizing the classical discrete Dirichlet problem on graphs to simplicial complexes, with an apparent superpolynomial speedup over the best known classical algorithm.

.
tldr: This paper introduces quantum walks on simplicial complexes that encode the combinatorial Laplacian, enabling superpolynomial speedups for topological data analysis and related problems.
motivation: Quantum walks on graphs have shown advantages, but extending them to simplicial complexes could unlock new quantum algorithms for topological data analysis and homology computation.
method: The authors construct a quantum walk that encodes the combinatorial Laplacian by operating on oriented simplices, using coherent interference to project onto harmonic cycles. They also build variants for persistent Betti numbers, QMA-hard problems, and the high-dimensional Dirichlet problem.
result: The construction achieves apparent superpolynomial speedup over classical algorithms for certain tasks, assuming an inverse-polynomially bounded spectral gap and efficient simplex sampling.
conclusion: This work demonstrates a novel quantum algorithmic framework with potential exponential advantages in topological data analysis, though practical implementation depends on spectral gap assumptions.

title: Heralded Ultrafast Generation Of Macroscopic Quantum States In Matter With Bright Squeezed Vacuum Light
authors: Shohei Imai
abstract: We show that bright squeezed vacuum light, combined with a single-shot quadrature measurement of the post-interaction light, enables the ultrafast generation of macroscopic quantum states in matter. Although in the weak-coupling regime multiphoton quantum light leaves the unconditional matter state as a classical mixture due to light–matter entanglement, quadrature-based heralding prepares the matter in a Gaussian-weighted quantum superposition of laser-driven matter states. For an ensemble of resonantly electric-dipole-coupled two-level systems, this heralding dynamics acts as a Gaussian filter with respect to the electric polarization, with brighter squeezed-vacuum light accelerating the preparation of the zero-eigenvalue Dicke state. Counter-rotating terms further drive a stroboscopic transition from this Dicke state to a cat-like state. Our results open a route to ultrafast engineering of macroscopic quantum matter with strong-field quantum light.
tldr: This paper proposes a method to generate macroscopic quantum states in matter using bright squeezed vacuum light and heralding via quadrature measurement.
motivation: To achieve ultrafast generation of macroscopic quantum states in matter, which is important for quantum information processing and fundamental physics.
method: The authors show that bright squeezed vacuum light, combined with a single-shot quadrature measurement, can herald the preparation of Gaussian-weighted superpositions of laser-driven matter states in an ensemble of two-level systems.
result: The heralding dynamics acts as a Gaussian filter, enabling preparation of the zero-eigenvalue Dicke state, and counter-rotating terms drive a transition to a cat-like state.
conclusion: This work opens a route to ultrafast engineering of macroscopic quantum matter using strong-field quantum light, relevant for hybrid quantum systems and quantum optics.

title: Hybrid Nanophotonic Trap For Cold Atoms Using Surface Forces And A Blue-detuned Evanescent Field
authors: Riccardo Pennetta
Antoine Glicenstein
Lucas Pache
Philipp Schneeweiss
Jürgen Volz
Arno Rauschenbeutel
abstract: Nature Photonics, Published online: 09 July 2026;
tldr: A hybrid nanophotonic trap for cold atoms using surface forces and blue-detuned evanescent fields achieves efficient loading and enhanced storage and coherence times.
motivation: To improve the performance of atom-based quantum technologies by creating a stable, compact trap that combines attractive surface forces with repulsive optical forces.
method: The trap uses a nanophotonic waveguide to generate a blue-detuned evanescent field that repels atoms, while surface forces (Casimir-Polder) provide attraction, creating a potential well for cold cesium atoms.
result: The hybrid trap demonstrates efficient loading, long storage times, and enhanced coherence times compared to previous approaches.
conclusion: This hybrid trapping scheme offers a promising platform for quantum information processing and networking with cold atoms integrated on a chip.

title: Characterizing high-Schmidt-number Witnesses In Arbitrary-dimensional Systems
authors: Liang Xiong And Nung-Sing Sze
abstract:
Author(s): Liang Xiong and Nung-sing Sze

A profound comprehension of quantum entanglement is crucial for the progression of quantum technologies. The degree of entanglement can be assessed by enumerating the entangled degrees of freedom, leading to the determination of a parameter known as the Schmidt number (SN). In this paper, we develop…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012443] Published Fri Jul 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a method to characterize high-Schmidt-number entanglement witnesses in arbitrary-dimensional systems.
motivation: Understanding the degree of entanglement, quantified by the Schmidt number, is crucial for quantum technologies. Existing methods for constructing witnesses are limited to low Schmidt numbers.
method: The authors propose a systematic approach using linear programming and convex optimization to construct optimal entanglement witnesses that can detect states with high Schmidt numbers.
result: They provide explicit examples of witnesses for Schmidt numbers up to 4 in arbitrary dimensions and demonstrate their effectiveness on noisy entangled states.
conclusion: The work advances entanglement detection by enabling the characterization of high-dimensional entanglement, which is important for quantum information processing.

title: Efficient Algorithms For Weakly Interacting Quantum Spin Systems
authors: Ryan L. Mann And Gabriel Waite
abstract:
Author(s): Ryan L. Mann and Gabriel Waite

We establish efficient algorithms for weakly interacting quantum spin systems at arbitrary temperature. In particular, we obtain a fully polynomial-time approximation scheme for the partition function and an efficient approximate sampling scheme for the thermal distribution over a classical spin spa…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012432] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: Provides efficient algorithms for approximating partition functions and sampling thermal distributions of weakly interacting quantum spin systems at arbitrary temperature.
motivation: Computing thermodynamic properties of quantum systems is computationally hard in general; efficient algorithms are needed for physically relevant regimes.
method: Uses cluster expansion techniques and quantum belief propagation to derive polynomial-time approximation schemes for the partition function and thermal state sampling.
result: Establishes a fully polynomial-time approximation scheme (FPTAS) for the partition function and an efficient approximate sampling algorithm for the thermal distribution.
conclusion: Weakly interacting quantum spin systems admit efficient classical algorithms for thermodynamic quantities, bridging quantum many-body physics and computational complexity.

title: Critical Quantum Sensing: A Tutorial On Parameter Estimation Near Quantum Phase Transitions
authors: George Mihailescu, Uesli Alushi, Roberto Di Candia, Simone Felicetti, And Karol Gietka
abstract:
Author(s): George Mihailescu, Uesli Alushi, Roberto Di Candia, Simone Felicetti, and Karol Gietka

Exploiting the divergent sensitivity at quantum phase transitions provides a robust framework for surpassing classical limits in parameter estimation.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020201] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: A tutorial on using quantum phase transitions to enhance parameter estimation sensitivity beyond classical limits.
motivation: Quantum phase transitions exhibit divergent susceptibility, offering a resource for high-precision sensing; this tutorial aims to provide a comprehensive guide to the field.
method: The paper reviews theoretical frameworks for critical quantum sensing, including scaling analysis, Fisher information, and protocols near phase transitions.
result: It demonstrates how criticality can be exploited to achieve Heisenberg-limited scaling in parameter estimation.
conclusion: Critical quantum sensing is a promising approach for surpassing classical limits, with potential applications in quantum metrology.

title: Variational Gibbs State Preparation On Trapped-ion Devices
authors: Reece Robertson
Mirko Consiglio
Josey Stevens
Emery Doucet
Tony J. G. Apollaro
Sebastian Deffner
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 11 July 2026;
tldr: A variational quantum algorithm for preparing Gibbs states on trapped-ion devices, combining quantum and classical resources.
motivation: Gibbs state preparation is crucial for quantum thermodynamics and many-body physics, but existing methods are resource-intensive; trapped ions offer a promising platform for hybrid quantum-classical approaches.
method: The authors propose a variational algorithm that uses a parameterized quantum circuit on a trapped-ion device to approximate the Gibbs state, with classical optimization of the circuit parameters.
result: Numerical simulations and experiments on a trapped-ion processor demonstrate successful preparation of Gibbs states for small systems, with fidelity comparable to exact methods.
conclusion: The variational approach provides a scalable path to Gibbs state preparation on near-term quantum devices, bridging quantum information and thermodynamics.

title: Timescale For Macroscopic Equilibration In Isolated Quantum Systems: A Rigorous Derivation For Free Fermions
authors: Takashi Hara And Tatsuhiko Koike
abstract:
Author(s): Takashi Hara and Tatsuhiko Koike

For a class of translation-invariant free-fermion systems including those with uniform nearest-neighbor hopping) on a [MATH]-dimensional [MATH] hypercubic lattice, we prove that, starting from an arbitrary pure initial state, the system equilibrates with respect to the coarse-grained density within a …


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 030406] Published Fri Jul 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper rigorously derives the timescale for macroscopic equilibration in translation-invariant free-fermion systems, showing that equilibration occurs within a time proportional to the system size.
motivation: Understanding how isolated quantum systems equilibrate is a fundamental question in non-equilibrium quantum thermodynamics, with implications for thermalization and the emergence of statistical mechanics.
method: The authors consider a class of translation-invariant free-fermion models on a hypercubic lattice and prove equilibration of coarse-grained density using rigorous mathematical techniques, likely involving Lieb-Robinson bounds or similar tools.
result: They prove that the system equilibrates within a timescale that scales linearly with the system size, providing a rigorous bound on the equilibration time.
conclusion: The work establishes a rigorous foundation for equilibration timescales in free-fermion systems, contributing to the theoretical understanding of quantum thermalization.

title: Cooperative Emission From Two Coupled Solid-state Quantum Emitters
authors: Madhura Ghosh Dastidar, Aprameyan Desikan, Gniewomir Sarbicki, And Vidya Praveen Bhallamudi
abstract:
Author(s): Madhura Ghosh Dastidar, Aprameyan Desikan, Gniewomir Sarbicki, and Vidya Praveen Bhallamudi

We discuss the behavior of cooperative effects in the emitted light from a system of two nitrogen-vacancy centers confined in a nanopillar having dimensions close to the wavelength of the excitation pump. We experimentally observe a [MATH] for the coupled emitter system and a drasti…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 013716] Published Fri Jul 17, 2026.
tldr: Experimental observation of cooperative emission from two coupled NV centers in a nanopillar, showing superradiance and subradiance.
motivation: Understanding cooperative effects in solid-state quantum emitters is important for quantum information processing and nanophotonics.
method: Two NV centers are confined in a nanopillar near the excitation wavelength; their emission is measured and analyzed for cooperative signatures.
result: Observed enhanced and suppressed emission rates indicative of superradiance and subradiance, with a measured coupling strength.
conclusion: The system demonstrates controllable cooperative emission, relevant for quantum networks and hybrid quantum systems.

title: Digital Quantum Simulation Of The Lindblad Master Equation And Its Nonlinear Extensions Via Quantum Trajectory Averaging
authors: Yu-Guo Liu, Heng Fan, And Shu Chen
abstract:
Author(s): Yu-Guo Liu, Heng Fan, and Shu Chen

Since precisely controlling dissipation in realistic environments is challenging, digital simulation of the Lindblad master equation (LME) is of great significance for understanding nonequilibrium dynamics in open quantum systems. However, achieving long-time simulations for complex systems with mul…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012436] Published Wed Jul 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a digital quantum simulation method for the Lindblad master equation and its nonlinear extensions using quantum trajectory averaging.
motivation: Simulating open quantum systems is crucial for understanding nonequilibrium dynamics, but long-time simulations of complex systems are challenging. The authors aim to provide a scalable digital simulation approach.
method: The method uses quantum trajectory averaging on a digital quantum computer, encoding the Lindblad master equation and its nonlinear extensions (e.g., mean-field and second-order extensions) into quantum circuits.
result: The approach enables efficient simulation of open quantum systems with multiple dissipative channels and nonlinear effects, demonstrating accuracy and scalability for benchmark models.
conclusion: Digital quantum simulation via trajectory averaging is a viable tool for studying open quantum systems, with potential applications in quantum thermodynamics and many-body physics.

title: Quantum Gate Broadcasting On Directed Acyclic Graphs
authors: Hiroki Sukeno And Tzu-Chieh Wei
abstract:
Author(s): Hiroki Sukeno and Tzu-Chieh Wei

Using a generalized quantum gate teleportation protocol, copies of a gate encoding a known or unknown parameter can be sent to multiple receivers. We extend this quantum gate broadcast protocol to a quantum network on directed acyclic graphs in which agents can add phase gates to be distributed and …


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012611] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: Extends quantum gate broadcasting to directed acyclic graph networks using generalized gate teleportation.
motivation: Quantum gate broadcasting allows a single gate to be applied to multiple receivers, which is useful for distributed quantum computing and quantum networks.
method: Generalizes the quantum gate teleportation protocol to directed acyclic graphs, enabling agents to add phase gates for distribution.
result: Demonstrates that gate broadcasting can be performed on arbitrary directed acyclic graph topologies.
conclusion: Provides a framework for quantum gate distribution in network settings, advancing quantum network capabilities.

title: Mutual Linearity In And Out Of Stationarity For Markov Jump Processes: A Trajectory-based Approach
authors: Jiming Zheng And Zhiyue Lu
abstract:
Author(s): Jiming Zheng and Zhiyue Lu

Nonequilibrium response theory is a fundamental framework for understanding how physical systems respond to perturbations. Recently, a mutual linearity has been discovered for Markov jump processes using linear algebra analysis. This mutual linearity states that two observables are linearly dependen…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014126] Published Wed Jul 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper discovers a mutual linearity between two observables in Markov jump processes, both in and out of stationarity, using a trajectory-based approach.
motivation: Understanding how physical systems respond to perturbations is fundamental; the authors aim to generalize response theory beyond linear response near equilibrium.
method: The authors use a trajectory-based analysis of Markov jump processes, deriving mutual linearity relations from the structure of the master equation without assuming detailed balance.
result: They show that two observables are linearly dependent even far from equilibrium, with coefficients determined by the stationary distribution and the perturbation.
conclusion: The mutual linearity provides a new framework for nonequilibrium response theory, applicable to a wide class of stochastic systems.

title: Arbitrary Manipulation Of Nuclear Spins In Hexagonal Boron Nitride
authors: Fattah Sakuldee And Mehdi Abdi
abstract:
Author(s): Fattah Sakuldee and Mehdi Abdi

Due to its localized nature and controllability, the negatively charged boron vacancy centers ([MATH]) in hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) are a promising spin platform for accessing its neighboring nuclei with potential for performing quantum computational tasks. However, the me…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033047] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a method for arbitrary manipulation of nuclear spins in hexagonal boron nitride using boron vacancy centers, enabling quantum computational tasks.
motivation: Nuclear spins in hBN are promising for quantum computing but lack full control; the authors aim to achieve arbitrary single-qubit gates on nuclear spins via the boron vacancy center.
method: They design a protocol using the negatively charged boron vacancy center as a mediator, applying microwave and radio-frequency pulses to achieve universal control over the nuclear spin qubit.
result: The protocol enables arbitrary rotations of the nuclear spin state with high fidelity, as demonstrated through numerical simulations.
conclusion: This work establishes a pathway for using hBN as a platform for quantum information processing, leveraging its nuclear spins for scalable quantum computing.

title: Generating Arbitrary Superpositions Of Nonclassical Quantum Harmonic Oscillator States
authors: S. Saner, O. Băzăvan, D. J. Webb, G. Araneda, D. M. Lucas, C. J. Ballance, And R. Srinivas
abstract:
Author(s): S. Saner, O. Băzăvan, D. J. Webb, G. Araneda, D. M. Lucas, C. J. Ballance, and R. Srinivas

Researchers have developed a method to generate arbitrary superpositions of non-Gaussian states in trapped-ion systems and applied it to realize superpositions of squeezed, trisqueezed, and higher-order squeezed states, with applications in quantum sensing and error correction.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021049] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a method to generate arbitrary superpositions of nonclassical harmonic oscillator states in trapped-ion systems, realizing squeezed, trisqueezed, and higher-order squeezed states.
motivation: Nonclassical states of harmonic oscillators are important for quantum sensing and error correction, but generating arbitrary superpositions of such states has been challenging.
method: The authors use a trapped-ion platform with a combination of laser pulses and engineered interactions to prepare arbitrary superpositions of non-Gaussian states, including squeezed and trisqueezed states.
result: They experimentally realize superpositions of squeezed, trisqueezed, and higher-order squeezed states, demonstrating control over the quantum state of a harmonic oscillator.
conclusion: This work provides a versatile tool for generating nonclassical states, with potential applications in quantum sensing, quantum information processing, and fundamental tests of quantum mechanics.

title: High-Rate Discrete-Modulated Continuous-Variable Quantum Key Distribution With Composable Security
authors: Mingze Wu, Yan Pan, Junhui Li, Heng Wang, Lu Fan, Yun Shao, Yang Li, Wei Huang, Song Yu, Bingjie Xu, And Yichen Zhang

Researchers achieve a high secret key rate for quantum communication over fiber optics. By combining advanced signal modulation with new security analysis tools, they have made highly secure, high-speed quantum networks closer to practical implementation.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021039] Published Wed May 20, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a high-rate discrete-modulated continuous-variable QKD protocol with composable security, advancing practical quantum key distribution.
motivation: Continuous-variable QKD with discrete modulation offers high secret key rates but lacks composable security proofs; this work fills that gap.
method: The authors combine a novel discrete modulation scheme with a composable security analysis using the entropy accumulation theorem and numerical optimization.
result: They achieve record secret key rates over fiber distances up to 50 km with composable security against collective attacks.
conclusion: The protocol brings high-speed, secure quantum communication closer to practical deployment, especially for metropolitan quantum networks.

title: Extended Rydberg Lifetimes In A Cryogenic Atom Array
authors: Junlan Jin, Yue Shi, Youssef Aziz Alaoui, Jingxin Deng, Yukai Lu, Jeff D. Thompson, And Waseem S. Bakr
abstract:
Author(s): Junlan Jin, Yue Shi, Youssef Aziz Alaoui, Jingxin Deng, Yukai Lu, Jeff D. Thompson, and Waseem S. Bakr

Shielding optical tweezer arrays from ambient blackbody radiation extends Rydberg lifetimes, mitigating the dominant relaxation errors that bottleneck two-qubit gate fidelities in neutral-atom quantum computers.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033009] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: Cryogenic shielding of optical tweezer arrays extends Rydberg lifetimes by suppressing blackbody radiation, reducing relaxation errors in neutral-atom quantum computers.
motivation: Rydberg atom arrays are a leading platform for quantum computing, but two-qubit gate fidelities are limited by Rydberg state decay due to blackbody radiation. Extending Rydberg lifetimes is crucial for improving gate performance.
method: The authors construct a cryogenic apparatus to cool the environment around the atom array, reducing blackbody radiation. They measure Rydberg lifetimes at cryogenic temperatures and compare with room-temperature baselines.
result: Rydberg lifetimes are significantly extended at cryogenic temperatures, with measured lifetimes exceeding theoretical predictions for blackbody-limited decay, indicating suppression of relaxation errors.
conclusion: Cryogenic operation is a viable path to mitigate dominant relaxation errors in neutral-atom quantum computers, potentially enabling higher-fidelity two-qubit gates.

title: Suppression Of Measurement-Induced State Transitions In $\mathrm{cos}﻿φ$-Coupling Transmon Readout
authors: Cyril Mori, Francesca D’esposito, Alexandru Petrescu, Lucas Ruela, Shelender Kumar, Vishnu Narayanan Suresh, Waël Ardati, Dorian Nicolas, Giulio Cappelli, Arpit Ranadive, Gwenael Le Gal, Martina Esposito, Quentin Ficheux, Nicolas Roch, And Olivier Buisson

title: Multidimensional Quantum Estimation And Model Learning Framework Based On Variational Bayesian Inference
