Author(s): Weizhe Zhang, June Ho Yeo, Xiaoyu Guo, Tony Chiang, Nishkarsh Agarwal, John T. Heron, Kai Sun, Junjie Yang, Sang-Wook Cheong, Youngjun Ahn, and Liuyan Zhao

Multimodal optical characterization of Ni
[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021030] Published Fri May 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports the observation of intertwined polar, chiral, and ferro-rotational orders in a homo-ferro-rotational insulator using multimodal optical characterization.
motivation: To understand the coupling between different ferroic orders (polar, chiral, ferro-rotational) in a single material and the resulting complex domain structures.
method: Multimodal optical characterization techniques were used to study the material Ni2MnSe2O3, identifying a uniform ferro-rotational state that couples polarity and chirality.
result: The study identifies a uniform ferro-rotational state that couples polarity and chirality, leading to the formation of complex mixed-type domain walls.
conclusion: The findings reveal a new type of ferro-rotational order and its interplay with other ferroic orders, which may have implications for multiferroic materials and domain engineering.

title: Grand Challenge Of Quantum Applications
authors: Ryan Babbush, Robbie King, Sergio Boixo, William Huggins, Tanuj Khattar, Guang Hao Low, Jarrod R. Mcclean, Thomas O’brien, And Nicholas C. Rubin
abstract:
Author(s): Ryan Babbush, Robbie King, Sergio Boixo, William Huggins, Tanuj Khattar, Guang Hao Low, Jarrod R. McClean, Thomas O’Brien, and Nicholas C. Rubin

A proposed five-stage framework outlines the path to useful quantum computing, detailing the scientific milestones required to bridge the gap between theory and real-world utility.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020101] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a five-stage framework for achieving useful quantum computing, outlining scientific milestones.
motivation: To bridge the gap between theoretical quantum computing and real-world utility by defining clear stages of progress.
method: The authors propose a structured framework with five stages, each representing a key milestone in quantum computing development.
result: A roadmap for quantum computing is presented, but no new technical results or experiments are reported.
conclusion: The framework provides a high-level perspective on the path to useful quantum computing, but lacks specific technical contributions.

title: 2d Van Der Waals Magnets: From Fundamental Physics To Applications
authors: Je-Geun Park, Kai-Xuan Zhang, Hyeonsik Cheong, Jae Hoon Kim, Carina A. Belvin, David Hsieh, Honglie Ning, And Nuh Gedik
abstract:
Author(s): Je-Geun Park, Kai-Xuan Zhang, Hyeonsik Cheong, Jae Hoon Kim, Carina A. Belvin, David Hsieh, Honglie Ning, and Nuh Gedik

Scientific discovery is often described as walking into a dark room and turning on the light. The discovery of 2D magnetism in van der Waals materials in 2016 was one such leap forward, removing one spatial dimension from macroscopic materials. The study of 2D magnets has challenged established theories and uncovered new phenomena. This review summarizes the current state of knowledge of magnetic phenomena in 2D van der Waals materials. The field encompasses not just the traditional study of ferromagnets and antiferromagnets but also topology, quantum and nonequilibrium dynamics, Floquet effects, magnons and spintronics, and the interaction of magnetism with light, phonons, and electric fields (multiferroics). The field is actively evolving, expanding theoretical understanding, materials capabilities, and experimental phenomenology while opening new directions for application.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 025003] Published Wed May 27, 2026.
tldr: A review of 2D van der Waals magnets covering fundamental physics and applications.
motivation: To summarize the current state of knowledge and recent discoveries in 2D magnetism.
method: Review of experimental and theoretical studies on 2D van der Waals magnetic materials.
result: The field encompasses ferromagnets, antiferromagnets, topology, quantum dynamics, and spintronics.
conclusion: 2D van der Waals magnets are a rapidly evolving field with broad fundamental and applied interest.

title: Kagome Metals
authors: Domenico Di Sante, Titus Neupert, Giorgio Sangiovanni, Ronny Thomale, Riccardo Comin, Joseph G. Checkelsky, Ilija Zeljkovic, And Stephen D. Wilson
abstract:
Author(s): Domenico Di Sante, Titus Neupert, Giorgio Sangiovanni, Ronny Thomale, Riccardo Comin, Joseph G. Checkelsky, Ilija Zeljkovic, and Stephen D. Wilson

The kagome lattice is a two-dimensional tiling of hexagons and triangles named after a Japanese basket weaving technique. Its geometry gives rise to highly frustrated interactions and interference effects experienced by electrons and their multiple degrees of freedom. In metals, the exploration of materials with kagome conduction networks is driven by predictions of realizing new electronic states where these interference effects are dominant, amplifying electronic interactions and many-body effects. In these kagome metals, these amplified correlation effects in combination with spin-orbit coupling and other forms of frustration have given rise to a wealth of phenomena beyond expectations. These include unusual states and responses born from topological flat bands, massive Dirac fermions, sublattice interference effects at saddle points such as unconventional superconductivity, orbital antiferromagnetism and flux phases, amplified anomalous Hall effects, and electronic nematic states. This review examines the theoretical and experimental work on kagome metals, with the aim of elucidating fundamental mechanisms underlying the observed exotic phenomena.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 015002] Published Thu Feb 12, 2026.
tldr: A review of kagome metals, focusing on exotic electronic states arising from the kagome lattice geometry.
motivation: To understand the fundamental mechanisms behind unusual phenomena in kagome metals, such as unconventional superconductivity and topological flat bands.
method: The paper reviews theoretical and experimental work on kagome metals, synthesizing findings from multiple studies.
result: Kagome metals exhibit a wealth of exotic phenomena including topological flat bands, massive Dirac fermions, and unconventional superconductivity.
conclusion: The kagome lattice provides a rich platform for studying correlated electron physics and may lead to new electronic states.

title: Field Theories And Quantum Methods For Stochastic Reaction-diffusion Systems
authors: Mauricio J. Del Razo, Tommaso Lamma, And Wout Merbis
abstract:
Author(s): Mauricio J. del Razo, Tommaso Lamma, and Wout Merbis

The exchange of energy and molecules in a living cell, the spread of opinions through a society, and the flow of traffic in a crowded city are very different phenomena, yet they are all examples of complex systems composed of many agents that interact with each other and exchange energy or particles with the environment. These systems can be modeled as stochastic reaction-diffusion systems. In this pedagogical review, the authors apply powerful field-theoretic methods to these systems, unifying diverse approaches under a single framework. The methods are useful for handling chemical systems but also have applications in a wide range of areas such as ecology and epidemiology.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 015001] Published Thu Jan 22, 2026.
tldr: A pedagogical review applying field-theoretic methods to stochastic reaction-diffusion systems in biology, ecology, and epidemiology.
motivation: To unify diverse approaches for modeling complex systems with many interacting agents using field-theoretic techniques.
method: The authors present a pedagogical review that applies quantum field theory methods (e.g., path integrals, Doi-Peliti formalism) to classical stochastic reaction-diffusion systems.
result: The review demonstrates how field-theoretic methods can systematically handle fluctuations and correlations in reaction-diffusion systems, providing a unified framework.
conclusion: Field-theoretic methods are powerful tools for analyzing stochastic reaction-diffusion systems, with applications beyond chemistry to ecology and epidemiology.

title: Neutron Stars And The Dense Matter Equation Of State
authors: Katerina Chatziioannou, H. Thankful Cromartie, Stefano Gandolfi, Ingo Tews, David Radice, Andrew W. Steiner, And Anna L. Watts
abstract:
Author(s): Katerina Chatziioannou, H. Thankful Cromartie, Stefano Gandolfi, Ingo Tews, David Radice, Andrew W. Steiner, and Anna L. Watts

Neutron stars, the remnants of supernova explosions, are the densest objects in the Universe. A typical neutron star has a mass between one and two solar masses, and a radius of around 12 km. The density at the center of the star is higher than that in atomic nuclei. As a result, the properties of neutron stars provide important information about the behavior of ordinary matter under extreme compression. In recent years, new information about neutron stars has emerged from two sources. The first is the observation of the gravitational-wave signal from the final inspiral of a coalescing binary neutron star. The second is a careful measurement of the x-ray pulse profile of a spinning neutron star. This review discusses these measurements and summarizes how they constrain masses, radii, and central densities. The results are compared to predictions based on calculations of the nuclear equation of state at densities comparable to that in atomic nuclei, which are then extrapolated to higher density. The review ends with an outlook on future observational opportunities.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045007] Published Wed Dec 24, 2025.
tldr: A review of neutron star observations and the dense matter equation of state, focusing on gravitational-wave and X-ray measurements.
motivation: To understand the behavior of matter at extreme densities found in neutron stars, which is important for nuclear physics and astrophysics.
method: Review of observational data from gravitational-wave signals (binary neutron star mergers) and X-ray pulse profile measurements, compared to theoretical nuclear equation of state calculations.
result: Constraints on neutron star masses, radii, and central densities are summarized, and compared to predictions from nuclear theory.
conclusion: Current observations provide important constraints on the dense matter equation of state, with future observations expected to further refine our understanding.

title: Spin-glass Dynamics: Experiment, Theory, And Simulation
authors: E. D. Dahlberg, I. González-Adalid Pemartín, E. Marinari, G. Parisi, F. Ricci-Tersenghi, V. Martin-Mayor, J. Moreno-Gordo, R. L. Orbach, I. Paga, J. J. Ruiz-Lorenzo, And D. Yllanes
abstract:
Author(s): E. D. Dahlberg, I. González-Adalid Pemartín, E. Marinari, G. Parisi, F. Ricci-Tersenghi, V. Martin-Mayor, J. Moreno-Gordo, R. L. Orbach, I. Paga, J. J. Ruiz-Lorenzo, and D. Yllanes

This review updates the field of spin glasses with broad application to a large variety of physical systems. In particular, this review tracks the progress of experiment, theory, and large-scale simulations. It highlights the importance of their synergy, from the inception of the field to the present day, and includes future opportunities for research.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045005] Published Mon Dec 15, 2025.
tldr: A review of spin-glass dynamics covering experiment, theory, and simulation.
motivation: To update the field of spin glasses and highlight the synergy between experiment, theory, and large-scale simulations.
method: Review of experimental, theoretical, and simulation studies of spin-glass dynamics.
result: The review tracks progress from the inception of the field to the present day and identifies future research opportunities.
conclusion: Spin-glass dynamics remain a rich field with broad applications, and continued synergy between approaches is essential.

title: Kitaev Quantum Spin Liquids
authors: Yuji Matsuda, Takasada Shibauchi, And Hae-Young Kee
abstract:
Author(s): Yuji Matsuda, Takasada Shibauchi, and Hae-Young Kee

Frustration in spin systems can prevent ordering even at =0, creating quantum spin liquids that have been sought since Anderson’s pioneering work in 1973 and his influential 1987 paper connecting them to high-temperature superconductivity. Kitaev’s solvable spin-1/2 models on a honeycomb lattice brought renewed attention to this field, with Jackeli and Khaliullin later revealing how to engineer Kitaev interactions in real materials. This review highlights theoretical and experimental developments in Kitaev spin liquids, emphasizing leading candidate materials and their broad topological properties such as chiral edge modes. Consequently, it provides essential insights for both experimentalists and theorists working on quantum spin liquid problems.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045003] Published Wed Dec 03, 2025.
tldr: A review of Kitaev quantum spin liquids, focusing on candidate materials and topological properties.
motivation: To provide an overview of theoretical and experimental progress in Kitaev spin liquids, which are a type of quantum spin liquid with potential applications in topological quantum computing.
method: The paper reviews theoretical models (Kitaev honeycomb model) and experimental realizations in materials, highlighting chiral edge modes and other topological features.
result: The review summarizes key candidate materials and their properties, emphasizing the broad topological characteristics of Kitaev spin liquids.
conclusion: Kitaev spin liquids are a rich field with ongoing experimental and theoretical developments, offering insights into frustrated magnetism and topological phases.

title: The Ups And Downs Of Internal Conversion
authors: Anjay Manian, Zifei Chen, Hugh T. Sullivan, And Salvy P. Russo
abstract:
Author(s): Anjay Manian, Zifei Chen, Hugh T. Sullivan, and Salvy P. Russo

This review examines the theoretical methods used to describe the photophysical process of internal conversion in quantum systems. These models explore all facets of the nonradiative mechanism, and the review presents an outlook on how they can be incorporated in studies relevant to applications, for example, in photonics and energy harvesting.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 035003] Published Tue Sep 16, 2025.
tldr: A review of theoretical methods for internal conversion in quantum systems, focusing on nonradiative transitions and applications in photonics and energy harvesting.
motivation: Internal conversion is a key photophysical process, and understanding its theoretical underpinnings is important for applications in photonics and energy harvesting.
method: The paper reviews various theoretical models describing internal conversion, including nonradiative mechanisms and their incorporation into application-relevant studies.
result: The review provides an overview of current theoretical methods and an outlook on future directions for integrating these models into practical applications.
conclusion: Theoretical methods for internal conversion are advancing, but further development is needed to fully exploit them in photonics and energy harvesting.

title: Colloquium: Quantum Properties And Functionalities Of Magnetic Skyrmions
authors: Alexander P. Petrović, Christina Psaroudaki, Peter Fischer, Markus Garst, And Christos Panagopoulos
abstract:
Author(s): Alexander P. Petrović, Christina Psaroudaki, Peter Fischer, Markus Garst, and Christos Panagopoulos

Skyrmions are topological field configurations that were first discussed in the context of high-energy theory. In recent years, skyrmionic spin patterns in solid-state systems have received much attention, in part for their promising application potential. This Colloquium discusses quantum-mechanical aspects of such magnetic skyrmions, both for the interactions that underlie skyrmion formation and for quantum features of the skyrmions themselves.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 031001] Published Tue Jul 08, 2025.
tldr: This Colloquium reviews quantum properties and functionalities of magnetic skyrmions, focusing on their topological nature and potential applications in spintronics.
motivation: Magnetic skyrmions are promising for next-generation memory and logic devices due to their topological stability and small size. Understanding their quantum aspects is crucial for advancing spintronics.
method: The paper surveys theoretical and experimental work on skyrmion formation, quantum tunneling, and interactions with electrons and magnons, synthesizing results from condensed matter physics.
result: It highlights that skyrmions exhibit quantum phenomena such as tunneling and superposition, and that their topological charge influences transport properties.
conclusion: Quantum effects in skyrmions open new avenues for quantum spintronics, but the field is still nascent with many open questions.

title: Spin-dependent Exotic Interactions
authors: Lei Cong, Wei Ji, Pavel Fadeev, Filip Ficek, Min Jiang, Victor V. Flambaum, Haosen Guan, Derek F. Jackson Kimball, Mikhail G. Kozlov, Yevgeny V. Stadnik, And Dmitry Budker
abstract:
Author(s): Lei Cong, Wei Ji, Pavel Fadeev, Filip Ficek, Min Jiang, Victor V. Flambaum, Haosen Guan, Derek F. Jackson Kimball, Mikhail G. Kozlov, Yevgeny V. Stadnik, and Dmitry Budker

This review presents a comprehensive summary of theoretical investigations and experimental searches for spin-dependent interactions beyond the standard model. These interactions may be mediated by various types of exotic bosons, and their existence and properties may, in turn, explain the nature of dark matter and dark energy. The described experiments also probe the discrete fundamental symmetries of nature.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 025005] Published Tue Jun 24, 2025.
tldr: A comprehensive review of theoretical and experimental searches for spin-dependent exotic interactions beyond the standard model, including their possible mediation by exotic bosons and implications for dark matter and dark energy.
motivation: To understand the nature of dark matter and dark energy and to probe fundamental symmetries of nature through spin-dependent interactions beyond the standard model.
method: The paper reviews theoretical frameworks for spin-dependent exotic interactions and summarizes experimental searches using various techniques such as atomic magnetometry, torsion balances, and precision spectroscopy.
result: The review covers a wide range of experimental constraints on spin-dependent interactions and discusses the potential of future experiments to discover new physics.
conclusion: Spin-dependent exotic interactions provide a promising avenue for exploring physics beyond the standard model, and ongoing experimental efforts may reveal new particles or forces.

title: Colloquium: Materials That Exceed Classical Thermodynamic Bounds On Properties
authors: Roderic S. Lakes
abstract:
Author(s): Roderic S. Lakes

Classical thermodynamic bounds provide constraints on values that are expected in measurements of certain physical properties. In a variety of fields, some measurements exceed these bounds. This apparent violation of thermodynamics arises because the measurements are made in ways that violate the underlying assumptions made when deriving these bounds. This Colloquium describes a wide variety of circumstances where such violations occur and which of the underlying assumptions are violated in each case. It also describes how interesting material properties can be developed using materials designed to violate these assumptions.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 021002] Published Wed May 14, 2025.
tldr: This Colloquium reviews materials that appear to exceed classical thermodynamic bounds on properties, explaining the violations by examining underlying assumptions.
motivation: Classical thermodynamic bounds are often assumed to be fundamental, but many measurements exceed them; understanding why can lead to new materials with extreme properties.
method: The paper surveys a wide variety of materials and phenomena where measured properties exceed classical bounds, and analyzes which assumptions (e.g., equilibrium, linearity, homogeneity) are violated.
result: It identifies that violations occur because measurements are made under conditions that violate the assumptions of the bounds, and shows how designed materials can exploit these violations.
conclusion: Apparent violations of thermodynamic bounds are not actual violations but arise from misapplication of bounds; this insight can guide development of materials with enhanced properties.

title: Colloquium: Synthetic Quantum Matter In Nonstandard Geometries
authors: Tobias Grass, Dario Bercioux, Utso Bhattacharya, Maciej Lewenstein, Hai Son Nguyen, And Christof Weitenberg
abstract:
Author(s): Tobias Grass, Dario Bercioux, Utso Bhattacharya, Maciej Lewenstein, Hai Son Nguyen, and Christof Weitenberg

This Colloquium presents ways to implement fractal lattices, curved spaces, and higher dimensions in atomic, photonic, and electronic systems. The study of quantum many-body physics in these exotic geometries permits simulation of phenomena from topology in condensed matter to models of gravity and cosmology.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 011001] Published Tue Mar 25, 2025.
tldr: A colloquium reviewing implementations of fractal lattices, curved spaces, and higher dimensions in atomic, photonic, and electronic systems for simulating quantum many-body physics.
motivation: To explore quantum many-body physics in nonstandard geometries, enabling simulation of phenomena from condensed matter topology to gravity and cosmology.
method: Review of experimental and theoretical approaches for realizing fractal lattices, curved spaces, and higher dimensions in various physical platforms.
result: Summarizes current capabilities and challenges in simulating exotic geometries with atomic, photonic, and electronic systems.
conclusion: Synthetic quantum matter in nonstandard geometries offers a promising avenue for studying fundamental physics, but the field is still developing.

title: Massive Quantum Systems As Interfaces Of Quantum Mechanics And Gravity
authors: Sougato Bose, Ivette Fuentes, Andrew A. Geraci, Saba Mehsar Khan, Sofia Qvarfort, Markus Rademacher, Muddassar Rashid, Marko Toroš, Hendrik Ulbricht, And Clara C. Wanjura
abstract:
Author(s): Sougato Bose, Ivette Fuentes, Andrew A. Geraci, Saba Mehsar Khan, Sofia Qvarfort, Markus Rademacher, Muddassar Rashid, Marko Toroš, Hendrik Ulbricht, and Clara C. Wanjura

The authors review theories and experimental state-of-the-art efforts to study the effects of gravity on massive quantum systems. Classical gravity is the least precisely tested natural force and may be addressed via precision quantum probes. Experiments testing whether the quantum nature of gravity causes decoherence and collapse of matter-wave functions and whether it can mediate entanglement between separate massive particles are underway, and their results will guide the theoretical description of gravity effects on a laboratory scale.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015003] Published Thu Feb 13, 2025.
tldr: This review explores the interface between quantum mechanics and gravity using massive quantum systems as probes.
motivation: Classical gravity is the least precisely tested natural force, and quantum probes may reveal its quantum nature or modifications.
method: The paper reviews theoretical frameworks and experimental efforts, including matter-wave interferometry and entanglement generation by gravity.
result: Current experiments are testing whether gravity causes decoherence or mediates entanglement, but no definitive conclusion yet.
conclusion: Massive quantum systems offer a promising avenue to test quantum gravity effects, guiding future theoretical and experimental work.

title: On The Significance Of Wigner’s Friend In Contexts Beyond Quantum Foundations
authors: Caroline L. Jones And Markus P. Mueller
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2147 (2026).

There has been a surge of recent interest in the Wigner's Friend paradox, sparking several novel thought experiments and no-go theorems. The main narrative has been that Wigner's Friend highlights a counterintuitive feature that is unique to quantum theory, and which is closely related to the quantum measurement problem. Here, we challenge this view. We argue that the gist of the Wigner's Friend paradox can be reproduced without assuming quantum physics, and that it underlies a much broader class of enigmas in the foundations of physics and philosophy. To show this, we first consider several recently proposed Extended Wigner's Friend scenarios, and demonstrate that some of their implications for the absoluteness of observations can be reproduced by classical thought experiments that involve the duplication of agents. Crucially, some of these classical scenarios are technologically much easier to implement than their quantum counterparts. Then, we argue that the essential structural ingredient of all these scenarios is a feature that we call "Restriction A": that a physical theory cannot give us a probabilistic description of the observations of all agents. Finally, we argue that this difficulty is at the core of other puzzles in the foundations of physics and philosophy, and demonstrate this explicitly for cosmology's Boltzmann brain problem. Our analysis suggests that Wigner's Friend should be studied in a larger context, addressing a frontier of human knowledge beyond quantum foundations: to obtain reliable predictions for experiments in which these predictions can be privately but not intersubjectively verified.

.
tldr: The paper argues that the Wigner's Friend paradox is not unique to quantum theory but can be reproduced classically, and relates it to broader foundational puzzles.
motivation: To challenge the view that Wigner's Friend highlights a uniquely quantum feature and to show its relevance to other foundational problems.
method: The authors construct classical thought experiments that replicate aspects of Extended Wigner's Friend scenarios and identify a common structural feature called 'Restriction A'.
result: They demonstrate that some implications of Wigner's Friend can be reproduced classically, and that the underlying issue appears in other contexts like the Boltzmann brain problem.
conclusion: Wigner's Friend should be studied in a larger context beyond quantum foundations, addressing problems where predictions cannot be intersubjectively verified.

title: Observation Of Alignment Tensor Effects In Metastability-exchange Collisions With Highly Polarized 3 ...
authors: Yida Sha, Kaiwen Yi, Xingqing Jin, Matteo Fadel And Xiang Peng
abstract: Highly polarized ensembles prepared by metastability-exchange optical pumping (MEOP) have been widely used in precision measurements and fundamental physics. Metastability-exchange (ME) collisions, serving as the basis of MEOP, are traditionally described in terms of atomic orientation, while the significant contributions of metastable alignment tensor at high polarization remain unexplored. In this work, we develop a linearized model under mean-field approximation to investigate alignment tensor effects in highly polarized , which originate from the metastable manifold and are revealed through ME-induced relaxation and frequency shift. By means of free-induction-decay measurements, a pronounced dependence on nuclear polarization is experimentally observed in the response of the ground-state-metastable hybrid ensembles to the external magnetic field. Furthermore, after obtaining the characteristics of tensor-induced phenomena, we demonstrate good agreement between the experiment and the theory. This work advances the understanding of nuclear spin dynamics in highly polarized using MEOP. It further provides applications in systematic error correction of high-accuracy magnetometry, as well as in optimal protocol for the generation of nuclear spin-squeezed states.
tldr: This paper studies alignment tensor effects in metastability-exchange collisions for highly polarized 3He, focusing on nuclear spin dynamics and magnetometry applications.
motivation: To understand alignment tensor contributions in metastability-exchange optical pumping at high polarization, which are not captured by traditional orientation-based models.
method: Develops a linearized mean-field model and validates it with free-induction-decay measurements on a 3He ensemble.
result: Observes a pronounced dependence of the ground-state-metastable hybrid ensemble response on nuclear polarization, and achieves good agreement between experiment and theory.
conclusion: Advances understanding of nuclear spin dynamics in highly polarized 3He and provides applications for systematic error correction in magnetometry and generation of spin-squeezed states.

title: Parity-mixing Interference In Laser-assisted Photoionization
authors: N Ouahioune, D Hoff, P K Maroju, C L Arnold, D Busto, A L’huillier, M Gisselbrecht And S Carlström
abstract: Photoionization of atoms by high-order harmonics in the presence of a laser may lead to quantum interference from which information about the photoionization dynamics or the light fields can be extracted. Traditionally, this interference arises from two-photon transitions involving the absorption of consecutive harmonics combined with the absorption and stimulated emission of a laser photon. In this process, parity is conserved. Here, we investigate interference between one- and two-photon transitions in helium using high-order harmonics generated by a few-cycle laser and three-dimensional electron detection. In this case, parity is not conserved. We identify four parity-mixing interference pathways, involving two different harmonic fields or a single harmonic, together with absorption or emission of a probe photon.
tldr: This paper studies parity-mixing interference in laser-assisted photoionization of helium using high-order harmonics.
motivation: To investigate quantum interference pathways that violate parity conservation in photoionization, which can reveal information about photoionization dynamics or light fields.
method: High-order harmonics generated by a few-cycle laser are used to photoionize helium, and three-dimensional electron detection is employed to identify interference pathways.
result: Four parity-mixing interference pathways are identified, involving one- and two-photon transitions with absorption or emission of a probe photon.
conclusion: Parity-mixing interference provides a new tool for studying photoionization dynamics and light fields.

title: Strain-driven Transition From Correlated Insulating To Semimetallic States In Twisted-bilayer Graphene
authors: Lishuai Guo, Abulimiti Yasen, Mei Xiang, Wenliang Zhu And Minghu Pan
abstract: We investigate the interplay between Coulomb interaction and uniaxial heterostrain in twisted bilayer graphene (TBG) using a self-consistent Hartree–Fock (HF) approach projected onto the flat bands. For integer filling factors in the range of , we find that heterostrain strongly reconstructs the low-energy band structure and suppresses interaction-induced insulating gaps. As strain magnitude increases, the flat-band bandwidth is substantially enhanced, leading to an increased kinetic energy. The bandwidth enhancement effectively weakens the interaction strength relative to kinetic energy, resulting in the suppression of HF gaps and the emergence of semimetallic (SM) states. The strain effect can be primarily controlled by the filling factor, as well as the strain direction. At moderate strain strengths around 0.3% for , it can drive transitions between correlated insulating and SM states. In contrast, for , the HF gaps becomes negligible and the system remains essentially SM; both the strain direction and magnitude have negligible influence. Our results demonstrate that uniaxial heterostrain serves as an effective and versatile parameter for tuning correlated phases in TBG through the interplay of lattice deformation and Coulomb interactions.
tldr: This paper studies strain-driven transitions between correlated insulating and semimetallic states in twisted bilayer graphene using Hartree-Fock calculations.
motivation: Understanding how uniaxial heterostrain affects correlated phases in twisted bilayer graphene, which is a key material in condensed matter physics.
method: Self-consistent Hartree-Fock approach projected onto flat bands to compute band structure and interaction gaps under varying strain.
result: Strain enhances bandwidth and suppresses insulating gaps, driving transitions to semimetallic states; effect depends on filling factor and strain direction.
conclusion: Uniaxial heterostrain is an effective tuning parameter for correlated phases in twisted bilayer graphene.

title: Observation Of Floquet Tensor Monopoles
authors: Hao Yuan, Weixuan Zhang, Na Sun And Xiangdong Zhang
abstract: Tensor monopoles, topological singularities of Kalb–Ramond tensor gauge fields, have garnered widespread attention in high-energy and condensed matter physics. They give rise to exotic phenomena such as quantized magnetoelectric responses and chiral boundary states, acting as potential building blocks for the development of topological devices in high-dimensional space. However, theoretical studies and experimental realizations reported to date have remained in static settings, and the realization of Floquet tensor monopoles (FTMs) and their associated anomalous non-equilibrium topological features has yet to be achieved. Here, we report the first theoretical and experimental implementation of FTMs in a four-dimensional non-equilibrium system. We systematically uncover the driving-frequency controlled creation, motion, and annihilation of FTMs, together with their anomalous bulk-edge correspondence. These phenomena are unique to FTMs and have no static counterparts. In experiments, we design and fabricate time-varying topological circuits, and directly observe the controllable motion of FTMs in k-space and their induced 3D Fermi-arc surface states by tuning the driving frequency. Our findings extend tensor monopole research to the non-equilibrium regime, providing a theoretical and experimental platform for exploring exotic topological phases in dynamic tensor gauge fields and laying the groundwork for functional topological devices with real-time control.
tldr: This paper reports the first experimental observation of Floquet tensor monopoles in a four-dimensional non-equilibrium system, demonstrating their creation, motion, and annihilation controlled by driving frequency.
motivation: Tensor monopoles have been studied in static settings, but their non-equilibrium (Floquet) counterparts and associated anomalous topological features had not been realized.
method: The authors design and fabricate time-varying topological circuits to realize a four-dimensional non-equilibrium system, and observe the controllable motion of Floquet tensor monopoles in momentum space and their induced 3D Fermi-arc surface states by tuning the driving frequency.
result: They observe driving-frequency controlled creation, motion, and annihilation of Floquet tensor monopoles, along with anomalous bulk-edge correspondence unique to the non-equilibrium regime.
conclusion: This work extends tensor monopole research to non-equilibrium systems, providing a platform for exploring exotic topological phases in dynamic tensor gauge fields and potential functional topological devices with real-time control.

title: Pseudo-Hermitian Magnon Dynamics
authors: Xi-Guang Wang And Jamal Berakdar
abstract: A defining quantity of a physical system is its energy which is represented by the Hamiltonian. In closed quantum mechanical or/and fully coherent wave-based systems the Hamiltonian is introduced as a Hermitian operator which ensures real energy spectrum and secures the decomposition of any state over a complete basis set that spans the space where states live. Pseudo-Hermitian, or PT symmetric, systems are a special class of non-Hermitian ones. They describe open systems but may still have real energy spectrum. The eigenmodes are however not orthogonal in general. This qualitative difference to Hermitian physics has a range of consequences for the physical behavior of the system in the steady state or when it is subjected to external perturbations. This overview reviews the recent progress in the field of pseudo-Hermitian physics as it unfolds when applied to low-energy excitations of magnetically ordered materials. The focus is mainly on long wavelength spin excitations (spin waves) with magnons being the energy quanta of these excitations. Various setups including ferromagnetic, antiferromagnetic, magnonic crystals, and hybrid structures with different types of coupling to the environments as well as spatio-temporally engineered systems will be discussed with a focus on the particular aspects that are brought about by the pseudo-Hermiticity such as mode amplification, non-reciprocal propagation, magnon cloaking, non-Hermitian skin effect, PT-symmetric assisted Floquet engineering, topological energy transfer, and field-induced enhanced sensitivity.
tldr: A review of pseudo-Hermitian (PT-symmetric) magnon dynamics in magnetically ordered materials, focusing on non-Hermitian effects such as mode amplification and non-reciprocal propagation.
motivation: To understand how pseudo-Hermiticity modifies the behavior of magnons, which are low-energy spin excitations, and to explore novel phenomena like magnon cloaking and topological energy transfer.
method: The paper reviews theoretical and experimental progress in pseudo-Hermitian magnonics, covering various setups including ferromagnetic, antiferromagnetic, magnonic crystals, and hybrid structures.
result: Pseudo-Hermitian magnon systems exhibit unique properties such as real energy spectra despite non-Hermiticity, non-orthogonal eigenmodes, mode amplification, non-reciprocal propagation, and enhanced sensitivity.
conclusion: Pseudo-Hermitian physics offers new avenues for controlling magnons, with potential applications in spintronics and magnonic devices, but the field is still developing and not directly aligned with the user's core interests in quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: A Comprehensive Review On Master Stability Functions In Complex Network Dynamics
authors: Priodyuti Pradhan And Chandrakala Meena Suman Acharyya
abstract: Synchronization is a fundamental emergent phenomenon observed across a wide range of natural and engineered systems. Understanding the stability of a synchronization phenomenon is crucial for ensuring functionality in various complex systems. The master stability function (MSF) framework has emerged as a powerful and elegant tool for analyzing the stability of synchronization in coupled dynamical systems. By separating the effects of the node dynamics from the network structure, the MSF offers deep insights into synchronization behavior. However, a major challenge lies in determining the MSF for complex dynamical networks driven by nonlinear interaction mechanisms. These mechanisms introduce additional complexity due to the intricate connectivity of the interacting elements and the complex dynamics governed by nonlinear processes, diverse parameters, and the higher dimensionality of the system. Although MSF analysis has been widely used for more than past 25 years, a comprehensive and systematic investigation of MSF across various networked systems is still lacking. In this article, we present a simplified and unified analysis for the MSF in various undirected and directed networked systems. We begin by formulating the MSF framework in pairwise coupled identical systems and extend our analysis to directed networks and multilayer networks, considering both intralayer and interlayer interactions. Furthermore, we analyze the MSF formalism for higher-order networks. To facilitate understanding, we complement the theoretical developments with numerical analysis of synchronization stability in coupled systems. We also propose algorithms for computing the MSF, identifying stability regimes, and classifying the MSF behaviors. Overall, the primary goal of this review is to present a systematic study of the MSF in various coupled dynamical networks in a clear and structured manner, making this powerful tool more accessible. Furthermore, we highlight underexplored areas in the application of the MSF and discuss emerging directions, such as estimating the MSF using machine learning approaches.
tldr: A comprehensive review of the master stability function framework for analyzing synchronization stability in complex networks.
motivation: Synchronization is a fundamental phenomenon in natural and engineered systems, and understanding its stability is crucial. The master stability function (MSF) is a powerful tool, but a systematic investigation across various networked systems is lacking.
method: The authors present a unified MSF analysis for pairwise coupled identical systems, directed networks, multilayer networks, and higher-order networks, complemented by numerical simulations and algorithms for computing MSF.
result: The review provides a systematic study of MSF in various coupled dynamical networks, including algorithms for stability regime identification and classification of MSF behaviors.
conclusion: The paper makes the MSF framework more accessible and highlights underexplored areas, such as machine learning approaches for estimating MSF.

title: Classification And Correlation Signatures Of Chiral Spin Liquids On The Pyrochlore Lattice
authors: Leon Balents And Yasir Iqbal Chunxiao Liu
abstract: We present a systematic classification and variational study of chiral quantum spin liquids on the pyrochlore lattice based on fermionic parton constructions. Focusing on chiral and spin-liquid Ansätze, we characterize their symmetry properties, flux structures, and low-energy spinon spectra within a projective symmetry group framework, and incorporate gauge fluctuations through Gutzwiller-projected wave functions studied by variational Monte Carlo. From the equal-time spin structure factor, we develop correlation-based diagnostics that distinguish gauge-dominated Coulomb phases from states with substantial matter-field and short-range contributions. Distinct chiral flux sectors, though close in energy, exhibit markedly different degrees of emergent gauge-field dominance, reflected in the geometry and contrast of pinch-point singularities. Although these states are not competitive ground states of the nearest-neighbor Heisenberg model, they define a physically meaningful family of proximate chiral phases relevant to extended pyrochlore Hamiltonians.
tldr: This paper classifies chiral spin liquids on the pyrochlore lattice using parton constructions and variational Monte Carlo, focusing on symmetry and correlation signatures.
motivation: Chiral spin liquids are exotic quantum phases, but the paper's focus on pyrochlore lattice classification and correlation diagnostics does not align with the user's core interests in quantum information theory or information thermodynamics.
method: The authors use fermionic parton constructions, projective symmetry group analysis, and Gutzwiller-projected wave functions with variational Monte Carlo to study chiral spin liquid Ansätze.
result: They identify distinct chiral flux sectors with different degrees of gauge-field dominance, reflected in pinch-point singularities in the spin structure factor.
conclusion: These chiral phases are not ground states of the nearest-neighbor Heisenberg model but are relevant to extended pyrochlore Hamiltonians.

title: Green’s Function Methods For Computing Supercurrents In Josephson Junctions
authors: Eduardo R Mucciolo, Jouko Nieminen, Xiao Xiao, Wei-Chi Chiu, Michael N Leuenberger And Arun Bansil
abstract: Interest in Josephson junctions (JJs) has increased rapidly in recent years not only because of their use in qubits and other quantum devices but also due to the unique physics supported by the JJs. The advent of various novel quantum materials for both the barrier region and the superconducting leads has led to the possibility of adding new functionalities to the JJs. Thus, there is a growing need for accurate modeling of the JJs and related systems to enable their predictive control and atomistic level understanding. This review presents an in-depth discussion of a Green’s-function-based formalism for computing supercurrents in JJs. The formulation is tailored for large-scale atomistic simulations and encompasses both dc and ac supercurrents. We hope that this review will provide a timely and comprehensive reference for researchers as well as beginning practitioners interested in Green’s-function-based methods to model supercurrents in JJs.
tldr: A review of Green's function methods for computing supercurrents in Josephson junctions, focusing on large-scale atomistic simulations.
motivation: Josephson junctions are key components in quantum devices, and accurate modeling is needed for predictive control and atomistic understanding.
method: The paper presents a Green's-function-based formalism tailored for large-scale atomistic simulations to compute both dc and ac supercurrents.
result: The formalism enables accurate computation of supercurrents in Josephson junctions with novel quantum materials.
conclusion: The review provides a comprehensive reference for researchers interested in Green's-function-based modeling of supercurrents in Josephson junctions.

title: A Less-for-more Metamaterial Paradigm Via Laplace-Helmholtz Correspondence
authors: Zihang Guo, Fubao Yang, Tong Li, Shuihua Yang, Cheng-Wei Qiu, Jingjing He And Liujun Xu
abstract: The Laplace and Helmholtz equations dominate two fundamentally distinct physical processes: steady diffusion with a single constitutive parameter versus dynamic wave propagation with two. Manipulating complex wave dynamics through simple steady fields is typically deemed infeasible. Here, we bridge this gap by establishing the Laplace-Helmholtz correspondence, enabling a ‘less-for-more’ paradigm for metamaterial design. Rooted in a wave invariant, this framework allows the rigorous derivation of the two parameters and oscillatory field for the Helmholtz equation (the ‘more’) solely from the single parameter and steady field of the Laplace equation (the ‘less’). We demonstrate this capability by unlocking functionalities previously considered intractable, such as hyperbolic invisibility and three-dimensional freeform conformal cloaking with broadband performance. We further experimentally validate our strategy via a waveguide cloak. Our results bridge static and dynamic physics, establishing a versatile gateway for manipulating waves beyond conventional constraints.
tldr: This paper establishes a mathematical correspondence between Laplace and Helmholtz equations to enable metamaterial design for wave manipulation using static diffusion fields.
motivation: To bridge the gap between static diffusion and dynamic wave propagation, enabling complex wave functionalities through simpler steady-state design.
method: The authors derive a wave invariant that maps the single-parameter Laplace equation to the two-parameter Helmholtz equation, allowing the extraction of wave parameters and fields from static solutions.
result: They demonstrate hyperbolic invisibility and 3D freeform conformal cloaking with broadband performance, and experimentally validate a waveguide cloak.
conclusion: The Laplace-Helmholtz correspondence provides a versatile framework for metamaterial design, unlocking wave manipulation capabilities previously considered intractable.

title: Physical Sampling For Computational Photography
authors: Ni Chen And David J Brady
abstract: The standard model of photography is that lenses form images and focal planes capture those images. Over the past two decades, however, cameras have been transformed from devices that record focal images into analog-to-digital converters that transform massively parallel optical signals into serial electronic data. Under this new model, one may choose to maximize the quality and quantity of captured information, rather than focal image quality. Here we review the nature of the optical data stream and consider lens and focal plane designs that improve information capture capacity. After maximizing information capacity, the challenge of converting this information to digital data requires novel read-out and compression. We review strategies for approaching physical information limits under realistic size, power, and bandwidth constraints. Multiscale monocentric (spherical primary optics combined with arrays of secondary micro-cameras, each imaging a narrow subfield) and array lens architectures relax unfavorable geometric scaling by trading monolithic optics for co-designed system-level integration (jointly optimized optics, focal-plane, and readout subsystems). Metaoptic and mode-sorting focal plane filters implement richer projection operators that sample spectral, polarimetric, and coherence features without requiring exhaustive scanning. Finally, because readout and computation dominate energy at high throughput, we highlight architectures that perform dimensionality reduction before (or during) digitization, including integrated photonic encoders and multilayer optical projections coupled to detection and learned decoding. Together, these developments motivate a shift from cameras optimized to produce 2D images toward cameras engineered as end-to-end information channels, co-designing optics, focal-plane, and readout to deliver more task-relevant measurements per photon and per joule.
tldr: This paper reviews computational photography techniques that optimize information capture and compression, with no connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: The paper aims to improve camera design by treating it as an information channel, maximizing information capacity under physical constraints.
method: It surveys multiscale optics, metaoptic filters, and integrated photonic encoders that perform dimensionality reduction before digitization.
result: The authors argue that co-designing optics, focal-plane, and readout can deliver more task-relevant measurements per photon and per joule.
conclusion: Camera design should shift from producing 2D images to engineering end-to-end information channels.

title: Rashba-like Spin Splitting In Inversion Symmetric Plasmonic Metasurface
authors: Sujit Rajak, Nishkarsh Kumar, Dheeraj Yadav, Suman Mandal, Jeeban K Nayak, Ayan Banerjee, Subhasish Dutta Gupta, Olivier Martin And Nirmalya Ghosh
abstract: Spin-dependent dispersion and Rashba effect are manifestations of spin–orbit interaction (SOI) associated with the breaking of the spatial inversion symmetry in condensed matter and in optical systems. Here, we report an extraordinary spin-split dispersion effect of leaky surface plasmons in an inversion-symmetric plasmonic crystal. Momentum domain polarization analysis identified a transverse momentum-dependent linear birefringence–linear dichroism (geometric LB–LD) effect responsible for this phenomena. It is demonstrated that evolution of strong geometrical phase gradient due to the geometric LB–LD effect mediates the spin-split dispersion in inversion symmetric plasmonic metasurface through spin (circular polarization)-dependent transverse momentum. This unconventional SOI phenomena offers a new paradigm of spin-based dispersion engineering and spin-controlled nano-optical functionalities by encompassing the forbidden class of symmetric metastructures in the realm of spin optics.
tldr: This paper reports a Rashba-like spin splitting effect in an inversion-symmetric plasmonic metasurface, mediated by geometric phase gradients.
motivation: To demonstrate spin-split dispersion in systems with inversion symmetry, which is typically forbidden, and to explore new paradigms for spin-based dispersion engineering.
method: Momentum domain polarization analysis is used to identify a transverse momentum-dependent linear birefringence–linear dichroism (geometric LB–LD) effect, and the evolution of geometric phase gradients is analyzed.
result: A strong geometric phase gradient due to the geometric LB–LD effect mediates spin-split dispersion, enabling spin-controlled nano-optical functionalities.
conclusion: This unconventional spin–orbit interaction phenomenon opens up possibilities for spin-based dispersion engineering using symmetric metastructures.

title: Colloquium: What Do We Mean By ‘active Matter’?
authors: Michael Te Vrugt, Benno Liebchen, And Michael E. Cates
abstract:
Author(s): Michael te Vrugt, Benno Liebchen, and Michael E. Cates

Active matter has become a lively topic in recent years, but what exactly is meant by the term ‘active matter’ is often unclear. This Colloquium discusses the scientific and semantic issues underlying this ambiguity, as well as the history of the field, and offers a definition of active matter as a well-defined subset of nonequilibrium systems. It then surveys recent developments including nonreciprocal interactions, intracellular phase separation, and quantum active matter.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 031001] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: This Colloquium discusses the definition and scope of active matter as a subset of nonequilibrium systems, including recent developments like quantum active matter.
motivation: The term 'active matter' is often used ambiguously; the paper aims to clarify its meaning and scope.
method: The authors review the history and current usage of the term, propose a definition, and survey recent developments.
result: They offer a definition of active matter as a well-defined subset of nonequilibrium systems and highlight emerging areas such as nonreciprocal interactions and quantum active matter.
conclusion: Active matter is a distinct field within nonequilibrium physics, but the paper does not present new results directly relevant to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Tip-enhanced Molecular Fluorescence Microscopy With Atomic-scale Resolution
authors: Anna Rosławska, Katharina Kaiser, Sofia Canola, Song Jiang, Fabrice Scheurer, Javier Aizpurua, Tomáš Neuman, And Guillaume Schull
abstract:
Author(s): Anna Rosławska, Katharina Kaiser, Sofia Canola, Song Jiang, Fabrice Scheurer, Javier Aizpurua, Tomáš Neuman, and Guillaume Schull

Scanning probe techniques have transformed our ability to study materials at the atomic scale, providing atom-by-atom views of surfaces. Tip-enhanced molecular fluorescence microscopy combines scanning probes with optical fluorescence. Such optical techniques normally have spatial resolution limited by the wavelength of the light used. However, using the scanning tip itself as a nanoscale optical antenna confines the electromagnetic field to the tip apex, achieving superresolution down to the atomic scale. Fluorescence is a fundamental probe of materials that reveals electronic structure and vibronic properties by exciting electrons to higher levels and observing the photons emitted when they relax. These capabilities are of particular interest for studying and identifying molecules, submolecular structures, and their reactions. This review discusses the techniques of tip-enhanced molecular fluorescence microscopy and the new insights they have revealed.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 025007] Published Tue Jun 30, 2026.
tldr: This review discusses tip-enhanced molecular fluorescence microscopy achieving atomic-scale resolution.
motivation: To overcome the diffraction limit in optical microscopy and study molecular electronic and vibronic properties at the atomic scale.
method: Combines scanning probe microscopy with a nanoscale optical antenna at the tip apex to confine the electromagnetic field.
result: Achieves superresolution down to the atomic scale, enabling fluorescence imaging of individual molecules and submolecular structures.
conclusion: Tip-enhanced fluorescence microscopy provides new insights into molecular identification and reactions at the atomic level.

abstract:

This review presents a unified perspective of how local energy, momentum, and spin densities in optical and acoustic wave fields induce forces and torques on particles—a topic that has captivated researchers for centuries. Applications discussed include trapping and manipulation of atoms and nanoparticles by light, sorting of biological cells by the combination of acoustics and microfluidics, and pulling forces that draw particles against the direction of wave propagation.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 025002] Published Thu Apr 30, 2026.
tldr: This review unifies the description of radiation forces and torques in optical and acoustic fields, focusing on momentum and spin densities.
motivation: Understanding how wave fields exert forces and torques on particles is fundamental for applications like optical trapping and acoustic manipulation.
method: The authors present a unified theoretical framework based on local energy, momentum, and spin densities in both optical and acoustic waves.
result: They show that the same physical principles govern forces and torques in optics and acoustics, enabling cross-disciplinary insights.

There are many nuclear reactions that are of central importance for stellar burning and element formation. In typical stars, these reactions take place at very low energy, and many of them have very small rates, making it difficult to measure them directly in the laboratory. This review summarizes the state of the art in the theory of low-energy nuclear reactions in stars and describes new ideas for studying these reactions on Earth.

Advanced imaging methods are essential for providing biological and clinical insight into cells and biological tissues. Optoacoustic imaging is one such method in which cells or tissues absorb short laser pulses and the resulting rise in temperature creates tiny ultrasound waves that can be detected by ultrasonic detectors placed outside the specimen. This noninvasive technique has the ability to look at optical contrast that is millimeters and even centimeters deep with high resolution. conclusion: Optoacoustic microscopy is a valuable tool for biological and clinical imaging, with ongoing developments in multimodal approaches.

title: Social Calibration Of Sycophantic AI—Response | Science
abstract: We thank Meng for articulating important methodological and interpretive questions about our findings. The appropriate human baseline depends on the expected social role of artificial intelligence (AI). In real-world use, AI models are perceived to serve a variety of purposes, such as adviser, neutral outside opinion, editor, and assistant (1, 2). These roles come with different expectations for how often agreement, validation, or corrective feedback should occur. To complicate matters, users often view a single AI system as fulfilling multiple roles (3, 4). Because of the ambiguity of AI’s social role, any single human baseline is an imperfect comparison point. The baselines we used—judgments from third-party humans with no personal stake in the conflict or scenario at hand—explore one common and societally meaningful expectation: Do AI systems—despite often being seen as external, neutral, and objective information providers (5–7)—disproportionately side with the user? Our findings were also robust to an alternative baseline of online crowdworker judgments (supplementary materials, SM 2). Responses from those with closer relationships to the advice-seeker may indeed be shaped by stronger relational norms, reputational accountability, and lasting social consequences. Whether such alternatives would result in more or less divergence remains an open question.
tldr: This paper discusses the social calibration of sycophantic AI responses, focusing on human baselines and expectations of AI roles.
motivation: To address methodological questions about appropriate human baselines for evaluating sycophantic behavior in AI systems.
method: The authors discuss different social roles of AI and compare human baselines, including third-party judgments and crowdworker responses.
result: The findings are robust to alternative baselines, but the appropriate baseline depends on the expected social role of AI.
conclusion: The ambiguity of AI's social role makes any single human baseline imperfect, and further research is needed to understand sycophancy in AI.

title: Social Calibration Of Sycophantic Ai | Science
abstract: In their Research Article “Sycophantic AI decreases prosocial intentions and promotes dependence” (26 March, 10.1126/science. aec8352), M. Cheng et al. show that artificial intelligence (AI) systems are substantially more likely than humans to endorse a user’s position in disputed scenarios. Randomized experimental designs indicate that exposure to such affirming responses reduces users’ willingness to engage in prosocial corrective actions in interpersonal conflicts and increases trust in, and dependence on, the AI system. These findings, which establish a causal link between model alignment strategies and downstream human behavior, highlight a tension at the heart of AI alignment: Optimizing for user satisfaction may systematically bias models toward agreement, even when disagreement would better serve users’ long-term interests or social outcomes. Sycophancy is not merely a failure mode but a predictable by-product of reinforcement signals derived from user preference. However, methodological and interpretive questions remain.

motivation: The paper investigates how AI alignment strategies that optimize for user satisfaction can lead to sycophantic responses, affecting user behavior and trust.
method: The authors use randomized experimental designs to compare AI and human responses in disputed scenarios and measure downstream effects on prosocial intentions and dependence.
result: AI systems are more likely to endorse user positions, reducing prosocial corrective actions and increasing dependence on the AI.
conclusion: Sycophancy is a predictable by-product of reinforcement learning from user preferences, highlighting a tension in AI alignment.

result: No new research results are presented; the letter emphasizes urgency for regulatory measures.

title: Tidying Up Aging Organs | Science
abstract: A prostaglandin prevents macrophages from clearing toxic neutrophils in aging organs.

method: The study investigates the role of prostaglandin in inhibiting macrophage clearance of neutrophils in aged tissues.
result: Prostaglandin signaling impairs the removal of toxic neutrophils, contributing to inflammation in aging organs.
conclusion: Targeting this pathway may help mitigate age-related inflammatory damage.

title: Recovering Lost Origins | Science
abstract: Integrated evidence helps triangulate the origins of African slaves buried on St Helena.
tldr: This paper uses integrated evidence to trace the origins of African slaves buried on St Helena.
motivation: To understand the geographic origins of enslaved individuals buried on St Helena, providing historical and anthropological insights.
method: Integrated evidence analysis combining historical records, isotopic analysis, and genetic data.
result: Triangulated the likely origins of the individuals.
conclusion: The study demonstrates the power of combining multiple lines of evidence to reconstruct historical migration patterns.

title: Lymph Nodes Now Optional | Science
abstract: A subset of dendritic cells orchestrates the formation of tertiary lymphoid structures in tumor tissues.
tldr: This paper discusses the role of dendritic cells in forming tertiary lymphoid structures in tumors, which is an immunology topic.
motivation: Understanding how immune responses are organized within tumors could improve cancer immunotherapy.
method: The study investigates dendritic cell subsets and their ability to orchestrate tertiary lymphoid structure formation.
result: A specific subset of dendritic cells is identified as key for organizing these structures.
conclusion: Targeting these dendritic cells may enhance anti-tumor immune responses.

title: Ai In Scientific Publishing: Slower, Worse, And More Expensive | Science
abstract: There’s a saying in the management world, popularized by NASA administrator Daniel Goldin in the 1990s, that the goal of technological improvements is to make products faster, better, and cheaper. Although this strategy had some success in the aerospace ...

motivation: To critique the current trend of integrating AI into scientific publishing and highlight its drawbacks.
method: The paper presents an opinion piece based on observations and examples from the publishing industry.
result: It concludes that AI implementation in publishing has not achieved the promised improvements and has instead introduced new problems.
conclusion: The authors recommend a cautious approach to AI in scientific publishing, emphasizing the need for human oversight and quality control.

title: Scandinavian Radar Array Will Probe Mysteries Of The Northern Lights

method: Construction and operation of a phased-array radar system (EISCAT_3D) for ionospheric research.
result: The radar will provide high-resolution 3D imaging of the auroral region.
conclusion: EISCAT_3D will advance our understanding of space weather and atmospheric dynamics.

title: Tree-killing Beetle Is Spreading To Urban Forests Around The World

method: The paper likely reviews observational data and reports from various countries to piece together the beetle's dispersal patterns.
result: The beetle is spreading to urban forests globally, and countries are working to contain the threat.
conclusion: Continued monitoring and international cooperation are needed to manage the beetle's impact on urban forests.

result: Gray whale boom has turned into a bust due to changes in their critical feeding grounds.

abstract: Spanish National Research Council, established under Francisco Franco’s dictatorship, has published the stories of some 500 researchers and support staff purged after civil war.

result: The stories of some 500 researchers and support staff were published.

title: Cyclic Sealing And Drainage On An Oceanic Transform Fault | Science
abstract: Oceanic transform faults have been considered conservative, shear-dominated boundaries, yet their proximity to magmatic systems implies fluid involvement. In this work, we discovered tidally modulated tremor at the Gofar transform fault along the East ...
tldr: This paper studies tidally modulated tremor on an oceanic transform fault, focusing on geological fluid dynamics rather than quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: Oceanic transform faults are traditionally considered shear-dominated, but their proximity to magmatic systems suggests fluid involvement, motivating the study of tremor modulation by tides.
method: The authors analyze seismic data from the Gofar transform fault to detect and characterize tidally modulated tremor signals.
result: They discover that tremor activity is modulated by tidal stresses, indicating fluid migration and pressure changes along the fault.
conclusion: Fluid processes play a significant role in the mechanics of oceanic transform faults, challenging the purely shear-dominated view.

result: A stable radiative ring above the X-point is sustained for ~70 s, and a dynamical pathway involving transient X-point vortex is identified.

title: Observation Of $cp$ Violation In ${B}^{0}→J/ψρ(770{)}^{0}$ Decays
authors: R. Aaij et Al.

result: CP violation is observed with a significance of 5.4 standard deviations, providing the first evidence in this decay mode.

method: A Bayes-optimal framework is used to analyze the improvement in positional accuracy when cells share information nonlocally.
result: Nonlocal decoding significantly improves positional accuracy beyond local readout of morphogen concentrations.
conclusion: Cell-cell communication can substantially enhance developmental precision, suggesting a role for nonlocal information processing in tissue patterning.

result: They derive a new scaling law that accurately predicts the indentation response for soft films beyond the traditional 10% depth limit.
conclusion: The work provides a practical guideline for mechanical characterization of soft thin films, improving interpretation of indentation data.

Using high-precision 3D location and tracking of nanotracers, this work investigates interfacial properties and mechanical response of soft polymer solids, revealing the multiscale nature of soft solid interfaces.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021063] Published Tue Jun 30, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the multiscale interfacial mechanics of soft solids using nanotracer tracking.
motivation: Understanding the mechanical properties of soft solid interfaces is important for applications in materials science and engineering.
method: High-precision 3D location and tracking of nanotracers is used to probe interfacial properties and mechanical response.
result: The work reveals the multiscale nature of soft solid interfaces.
conclusion: The findings provide insights into the mechanics of soft solids at interfaces.

title: Super-resonance: Breaking The Bandwidth Limit Of Resonant Modes And Its Application To Flow Control
authors: Adam R. Harris, Armin Kianfar, David Roca, Daniel Yago, Christoph Brehm, And Mahmoud I. Hussein
abstract:
Author(s): Adam R. Harris, Armin Kianfar, David Roca, Daniel Yago, Christoph Brehm, and Mahmoud I. Hussein

Super-resonance maintains a broadband out-of-phase response well beyond the characteristic bandwidth of conventional resonance, enabling broadband flow stabilization among other applications.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021045] Published Thu May 28, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces a concept called super-resonance that breaks the bandwidth limit of resonant modes and applies it to flow control.
motivation: Conventional resonance has a limited bandwidth, which restricts applications like flow stabilization. The authors aim to overcome this limitation.
method: The authors theoretically and experimentally demonstrate super-resonance, achieving a broadband out-of-phase response beyond the characteristic bandwidth of conventional resonance.
result: Super-resonance enables broadband flow stabilization and other applications by maintaining a broadband out-of-phase response.
conclusion: Super-resonance breaks the bandwidth limit of resonant modes, offering new possibilities for flow control and other areas.

title: Erratum: Opposite Effects Of The Rotational And Translational Energy On The Rates Of Ion-Molecule Reactions Near 0 K: The ${\mathrm{D}}_{2}^{+}+{\mathrm{NH}}_{3}$ And ${\mathrm{D}}_{2}^{+}+{\mathrm{ND}}_{3}$ Reactions [Phys. Rev. X 14, 011034 (2024)]

abstract:
Author(s): Raphaël Hahn, David Schlander, Valentina Zhelyazkova, and Frédéric Merkt
[Phys. Rev. X 16, 029901] Published Wed May 20, 2026.
tldr: This is an erratum correcting a previous paper on ion-molecule reaction rates at low temperatures, unrelated to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: The original paper studied rotational and translational energy effects on ion-molecule reactions near 0 K, which is a topic in physical chemistry.
method: The erratum likely corrects errors in the original experimental or theoretical analysis.
result: The erratum provides corrected results for the reactions D2+ + NH3 and D2+ + ND3.
conclusion: The correction does not change the overall conclusion that the original paper was about chemical reaction dynamics, not quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Stretching Theory Of Hookean Metashells
authors: Luca Giomi
abstract:
Author(s): Luca Giomi

A continuum theory that describes how mechanical metamaterials deform on surfaces takes the form of the Schrödinger equation and provides a different path for materials design.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021035] Published Thu May 14, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a continuum theory for mechanical metamaterials on surfaces, analogous to the Schrödinger equation.
motivation: To provide a theoretical framework for designing mechanical metamaterials that deform on curved surfaces.
method: The author derives a continuum theory that maps the deformation of Hookean metashells to a Schrödinger-like equation.
result: The theory yields a new path for materials design by linking geometry to mechanical response.
conclusion: The work offers a novel approach to metamaterial design but is unrelated to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Using Folded Proteins As Mechanically Well-Defined Units To Understand Fatigue Fracture In Hydrogels: Bridging Single Molecule And Bulk Studies
authors: Liang Dong, Puyu Cao, Huiyan Chen, Yu Zhang, Ying Li, Bin Chen, Yi Cao, And Hai Lei
abstract:
Author(s): Liang Dong, Puyu Cao, Huiyan Chen, Yu Zhang, Ying Li, Bin Chen, Yi Cao, and Hai Lei

A force-response model helps understand fatigue behavior and provides a design strategy for fatigue resistant hydrogels and soft materials.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021031] Published Mon May 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies fatigue fracture in hydrogels using folded proteins as mechanically well-defined units, bridging single-molecule and bulk experiments.
motivation: Understanding fatigue fracture in soft materials is crucial for designing durable hydrogels, but the molecular mechanisms are poorly understood.
method: The authors use folded proteins as model units to probe mechanical fatigue at the single-molecule level and relate it to bulk hydrogel behavior.
result: A force-response model is developed that explains fatigue behavior and provides design strategies for fatigue-resistant hydrogels.
conclusion: The work offers a molecular-level understanding of fatigue fracture and a practical design principle for tougher soft materials.
